text: The food was okay. Their interpretation of traditional German cuisine was rather adventurous. The service was disappointing. We had a time slot from 7:30 pm to 9:15 pm. That should have been enough time to place our order and perhaps even finish a three-course meal. Let's just say the view was fantastic and somewhat compensated for the long wait. The greeting was slow, then ordering took a while, and by the time the food arrived, we had enjoyed the view again. And when it came time to pay, we waited again. Our waiter seemed to spend inconsistent amounts of time with his guests, and we were simply unlucky. To top it all off, the restrooms left much to be desired in terms of cleanliness. It was a disappointing end to our visit to Berlin.
originalText: Das Essen war ok. Die Interpretation der Hausmannskost ist gewagt. Der Service war traurig. Wir hatten ein Zeitfenster von 19.30 Uhr bis 21.15 Uhr. In der Zeit sollte es ausreichen die Bestellung aufzugeben und ggf. sogar ein Dreigänge-Menü zu verspeisen. Sagen wir es so, die Aussicht war toll und hat uns über die längeren Wartezeiten etwas getröstet. Die Begrüßung ließ auf sich warten, dann das bestellen dauerte, bis das Essen kam haben wir die Aussicht erneut genossen. Und als es ans Bezahlen ging warteten wir wieder. Unser Kellner hat sich unterschiedlich viel Zeit genommen für seine Gäste und wir hatten wohl Pech. Zum Abschluss des Abends ließen auch die Toiletten bei der Sauberkeit zu wünschen übrig. Es war ein enttäuschender Abschluss für unseren Besuch in Berlin.

text:
Mixed feelings about this dining experience, so I’ll split it into two parts.

Service: At the end of the evening, I walked around to take in the view before heading to the exit. While doing so, I was intercepted by a waitress in a disrespectful way — he asked if I even had a table and what I was doing there. Keep in mind I was holding a digital camera, since I’d been taking pictures from the window at my table. He then told me I needed to move out of the way, apparently assuming I was standing there to take photos, which I wasn’t. I asked if it was okay to take a picture (the area was completely empty), and he said it was fine, just close to the window. I hadn’t even planned on taking one.

Overall, this interaction was unpleasant and put a damper on all the effort the rest of the team had put in that night. Afterward, I went back to the restaurant to ask for his name but couldn’t find him. I described her to Benny (the guy who assisted me that night) I described the other guy who intercepted me as — tall, slim, Italian-looking, with a beard — and we believe it was Miguel.

I’ve visited similar venues around the world, such as the one in Toronto, and I’ve never experienced such an odd, low-etiquette interaction from staff.

Food: Nothing out of this world, but the cocktail selection and wine pairing were good. I’d say the food overall is solid — not fine dining, not extraordinary, but well executed. I’d recommend it, and you can’t go wrong with the dishes I ordered.

View: Amazing.

We’ll take your comments back to the team so that such situations are handled more thoughtfully in the future.

The Sphere Tim Raue Team

text:
I’ve gotten used to being disappointed at restaurants. Blacksmith definitely takes pride in the quality of their ingredients. Took my 5yo, 9yo, and mother for lunch. We all shared Caesar salads and authentic dressing is what sold me to come here. The crab deviled eggs were out of this world(so thankful we got 2 orders). We wanted to try a lot so we got the crab bisque, hamburger, softshell crab sandwich, and cheesesteak.

Caesar dressing and the croutons were excellent. Crab bisque was what we expect from a good bisque. Softshell sandwich was a light crispy fry on it. Hamburger was wonderfully cooked. The filet cheesesteak was delicious! The way they do the cheese was nice, and different. I thought I would rather have a ribeye instead of filet for the cheesesteak but it was a nice surprise not having any chewiness at all. The onions, mushrooms, peppers, and cheese were great compliments. We couldn’t finish everything but I’m so happy we ordered all of it to try.

Our server, Emily, was wonderful and accommodating. I am really impressed with the quality and delivery of the cooking here. Not one dish was trying to do too much taking away from the quality of the ingredients. This lunch really made a good day into a great day.

Thank you Blacksmith! We all had a great and memorable experience.
ownerResponseText: Brian, thank you so much for the stellar review. We do absolutely take pride in what we do and it means the world to us when our guests notice. We are a Chef owned restaurant and we work hard to keep our focus on hand-made and guest friendly. Again, Thank you so much

text:
Three is not a great rating but I will tell you I'd go back again in a heartbeat. It felt like perhaps the kitchen was behind/slammed and making some rookie mistakes. Going to start with the negatives but there were positives.
Negatives: the stacked crispy eggplant was a mess. The eggplant was not at all crispy. Though it tasted ok, it was nothing but mush. There was so much boursin in between that it was all you could taste. Also, it's hard to understand why something like bread or toast points wouldn't be served with it.

One of us ordered the crabcake platter. The cakes were both burnt. The kitchen shouldn't have sent it and the server should've had a better eye. They were clearly burnt all over but the bottom was one solid color of near black. The potatoes with it were under seasoned.

The cream of crab was also disappointing. There was too much sherry in it and tasted over-reduced. Like perhaps it had been simmering for way too long the past couple days.

It was frustrating because you can tell that they are capable of putting out better food but too many things were poorly executed.

For the positives:
The crispy deviled eggs are amazing. Get them. Period.
Our server was very friendly and provided good service.
The setting is lovely, albeit a bit crowded inside.
Other than the deviled eggs, the shrimp risotto was a real hit.

Next time I'm in Berlin, I wouldn't hesitate to go there again but probably not on a busy Friday night.

text:
I don’t normally write reviews, but after our experience here, I felt I should—for the sake of others. I took my family of four here for dinner after seeing the nice photos online. It looked promising, but unfortunately, the consensus was that we all left very disappointed.

The service was poor from the start. Our server was snooty and rarely checked on us—we had to flag her down just for basic refills. When we politely asked if she could check on our food (which was taking quite a while), she responded with unexpected rudeness.

As for the food: overpriced and underwhelming. My wife’s salad looked like it came straight from a bag, and the crab cake didn't taste as a crab cake should. The brie platter was decent, but certainly not worth what they charged.

The whole place felt disorganized. Despite several visible empty tables, we were made to wait for a table. The host seemed flustered, even though the restaurant wasn’t busy. We waited at the bar and shared an appetizer—credit to the bartender, who was actually the only highlight of the evening.

We expected better, especially in a small town where service is usually more welcoming. Sadly, we won’t be returning and wouldn’t recommend this place to others.

text:
I stepped inside this establishment with the simple intent of utilizing the restroom facilities, fully prepared to compensate the venue for the facilities. Upon inquiring about the fee, I was met with a curt, categorical refusal by a young male employee who, I suspect, was merely an employee rather than the proprietor.

While the establishment is well within its legal rights to govern its property, this rigid approach represents a profound failure in the art of hospitality. True restaurateurs understand that today’s passerby is tomorrow’s devoted diner. By treating a polite inquiry with such cold indifference, the venue entirely missed an opportunity to convert a prospective patron into a future guest.

Such short-sightedness inflicts unnecessary damage upon the business's local reputation. Needless to say, I shall never patronize this establishment, nor can I recommend a venue that operates with such an ungenerous spirit.

text:
My husband and I stumbled upon this Indian restaurant in Berlin, and it turned out to be an incredible surprise! As Mexicans, we were craving bold, spicy flavors, and this place exceeded all our expectations.

The atmosphere is serene, cozy, and intimate, with beautiful decor inspired by Indian culture. From the moment we walked in, we felt welcomed. The waiter was exceptionally kind and patient, taking the time to guide us through the menu options.

We decided to try the Rogan Josh and Chicken Jahl Ferezi, both marked as spicy 🌶️. The spice level was perfect, not overpowering, just enough to be flavorful and enjoyable (the dishes come with a big portion of jasmine rice). We also ordered a garlic-based soup called Lasan-Shorba, which was absolutely delicious!

To accompany our meal, we had a garlic naan and a variety of drinks a berliner beer on tap and a russian cocktail called Caipiroska (made with vodka, lemon, sugar and ice). As a complimentary starter, they served us garlic toast with seeds and three different dipping sauces, all of which were fantastic (the green one was too spicy, but yummy!)

For dessert, we chose Gulab Jamun and Südseetraum, both of which were the perfect way to end our meal. To top it off, the restaurant surprised us with a complimentary drink of our choice. I had vodka, and my husband opted for tequila.

Every dish was bursting with flavor, the service was outstanding, and the overall experience was unforgettable. If you’re in Berlin and looking to try something different, we highly recommend this restaurant!

It’s a place where delicious food meets exceptional hospitality. Don’t miss it! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

text:
We went to Sorrel last Friday.

First let’s review the positive aspects. We didn’t have a reservation and they gave us a table and the team was friendly. Further, the atmosphere is very nice and cosy.

Now about the food, the appetisers were good but when the additional dishes arrived,  we got a shock when we spotted hair in two dishes. We informed the team about the issue and gave the dishes back. As you can imagine we weren’t able to enjoy the rest of our meal as we lost our appetite, so we paid and left.
It was a pity because we were so excited about the food and enjoying a nice dinner.

This situation should be looked at and improved as it’s  unacceptable for such a restaurant.
ownerResponseText: Hi Sarai, Thanks for coming by. I’m really sorry you found hair in two dishes. That’s unacceptable and not our standard. We’ve spoken with the team and are tightening prep and pass checks to prevent this. I understand it ruined the meal, and I’m sorry you left disappointed. We’d really like to understand this better / try to make things right. Could you please drop us a line at hello@sorrel.berlin so we can connect?

text: Well, to start off I was a Professional Chef in San Francisco as well as Los Angeles for over 17 years, one of them being Michelin star so I know food as well as how things can be done service wise.This place is nowhere near Michelin starred so the arrogance was ridiculously absurd in my and my Partners opinion. I was invited by a friend because I'm visiting Berlin. I wanted to switch the fried egg with a scrambled because I don't like fried eggs. The Server said they would ask if they would scramble instead of fry, the server came back and said they could but WON'T scramble the eggs. There was nothing else on that menu I could eat except the potatoes and Mussels which I was kinda forced to eat due to most of my party  already eating the food they ordered. I didn't want to make THEIR experience difficult. The mussels were VERY dry and it was hard to spoon the sauce onto it due to how it was served in the bowl. I ended up not eating much of them but my table mates didn't mind as much and partook in them anyway. It literally takes very little effort to scramble an egg and instead of being accommodating they choose to "Not scramble". The toast was decent and the Potatoes and Matcha I ordered were good but the experience absolutely left a bad taste in my mouth so I would never return to this restaurant. I've had way better experiences at other Breakfast and Brunch Restaurants in Berlin. I didn't desire to eat Mussels at 11am in the morning.
ownerResponseText:
Hi Michele,

I’m sorry about how we handled your request to have the egg scrambled. We should have communicated better and tried to find a workable solution. I hear your feedback on the rest of the experience and it’s clear we fell short for you. I’m sharing this with the team today so we can review our approach to modifications and the dishes you mentioned. Thank you for calling it out; we will use it to improve.

placeAddress: 136 Berlin Restaurant, Linienstraße 136, 10115 Berlin, Germany
text:
Peruvian-Italian cuisine sounds unusual at first, and that's precisely why we chose this restaurant. We were very curious to see if the concept could also deliver on flavor. And it definitely did.

Every single course was superbly coordinated, creative, and of a very high standard in terms of taste. Whether monkfish, Wagyu short rib, sauces, or essences, everything was incredibly refined, balanced, and prepared with meticulous attention to detail. The cuisine is undoubtedly the highlight and fully justifies the price point.

The interior is harmonious and fits the overall concept perfectly. The head chef deserves special mention; he personally visits the tables, explains the dishes, and is incredibly open, friendly, and charming. You can immediately sense the passion and dedication that has gone into this restaurant. The sommelier was also very attentive, knowledgeable, and open to feedback.

There is some room for improvement in the service. At times, there was a lack of attention, for example, when refilling wine and water glasses, setting the table, or with small details during the pouring process. Especially if the restaurant is aiming for a Michelin star, there's still room for improvement here.

Despite these minor shortcomings, we were very impressed with our evening overall. The quality of the food, the pleasant atmosphere, and above all, the charming personality of the chef make this restaurant a truly recommendable choice. The price-performance ratio is excellent, and we will definitely be back.
originalText:
Eine peruanisch italienische Küche klingt zunächst ungewöhnlich und genau deshalb haben wir uns für dieses Restaurant entschieden. Wir waren sehr gespannt, ob das Konzept auch geschmacklich überzeugen kann. Und das kann es definitiv.

Jeder einzelne Gang war hervorragend abgestimmt, kreativ und geschmacklich auf einem sehr hohen Niveau. Ob Seeteufel, Wagyu Short Rib, Soßen oder Essenzen, alles war unglaublich fein, ausgewogen und mit viel Liebe zum Detail zubereitet. Die Küche ist ohne Frage das große Highlight und rechtfertigt auch das Preisniveau vollkommen.

Das Interieur ist stimmig und passt sehr gut zum Gesamtkonzept. Besonders positiv hervorzuheben ist der Chefkoch, der persönlich an die Tische kommt, die Gerichte erklärt und dabei unglaublich offen, freundlich und charmant auftritt. Man merkt sofort, wie viel Leidenschaft und Herzblut hinter dem Restaurant steckt. Auch der Sommelier war sehr aufmerksam, kompetent und offen für Rückmeldungen.

Etwas Luft nach oben gibt es beim Service. Teilweise fehlte es an Aufmerksamkeit, etwa beim Nachschenken von Wein und Wasser, beim Eindecken des Bestecks oder bei kleinen Details während des Einschenkens. Gerade wenn das Restaurant einen Stern anstrebt, sollte hier noch etwas nachgebessert werden.

Trotz dieser kleinen Schwächen hat uns der Abend insgesamt sehr überzeugt. Die Qualität der Küche, die angenehme Atmosphäre und vor allem die charmante Art des Chefkochs machen das Restaurant zu einer echten Empfehlung. Das Preis Leistungs Verhältnis stimmt und wir werden auf jeden Fall wiederkommen.

text: My companion and I ordered the set menu for weekend brunch, which included French toast, eggs and labneh, trout with potatoes, fennel salad, and burrata. Unfortunately, we found everything to be overly acidic. The pickled jalapeños with the burrata were completely out of place; they were totally pointless and tasted of nothing. The fennel was okay, nothing special, the trout with potatoes was average, also a bit too acidic, and the labneh under the eggs was particularly disappointing. The French toast with its Calvados-flavored cream was at least sweet, but the overly acidic cream was a shame. For €70 for two people, I definitely expected much more and can't recommend this place. It's surprising that a brunch like this in Neukölln could be so underwhelming. The flat white was very bitter, which is why we didn't want a second drink. At least they offered free tap water, the restrooms were clean, and we tried the Sorrel. Perhaps we were just unlucky with the current menu.
originalText: Ich hatte mit meiner Begleitung zum Weekend-Brunch das Set-Menü mit French Toast, Eggs+Labneh, Forelle mit Kartoffeln, Fenchelsalat und Burrata. Wir fanden leider alles irgendwie übersäuert. Die eingelegten Jalapenos zum Burrata waren unpassend, das hat sich leider null gelohnt und schmeckte nach nichts. Der Fenchel war okay, nicht shocking, die Forelle mit Kartoffeln war normal, auch bisschen zu sauer und besonders das Labneh unter den Eiern war nix. Das French Toast mit einer alkoholhaltigen Calvados-Creme dazu war immerhin süß, aber die übersäuerte Creme war schade. Für 70 Euro für 2 Personen habe ich definitiv viel mehr erwartet und kann den Laden nicht weiterempfehlen. Dass ein Brunch dieser Art in Neukölln so ernüchternd sein kann ist überraschend. Der Flat White ist sehr bitter, weshalb wir kein zweites Getränk wollten. Immerhin gibt es Tap Water kostenlos, die Toiletten sind sauber und wir haben das Sorrel getestet. Vielleicht hatten wir einfach Pech mit der aktuellen Karte.
ownerResponseText: Hi Alina, thank you for your honest feedback and we're sorry the brunch wasn't quite right for you. We take the acidity balance you mentioned very seriously; it seems we didn't quite hit the mark there. We're reviewing the current menu and adjusting the seasoning and accompaniments accordingly. The price should reflect the taste. If you'd like, please get in touch so we can discuss it in more detail, and feel free to come back another time. Your feedback helps us refine the details, thank you.
ownerResponseOriginalText: Hi Alina, danke für dein offenes Feedback und sorry, dass der Brunch für euch nicht gestimmt hat. Vor allem die von dir beschriebene Säurebalance nehmen wir wirklich ernst, da haben wir offenbar nicht getroffen. Wir prüfen das aktuelle Menü und passen Abschmeckung und Begleitungen entsprechend an. Der Preis soll sich im Geschmack wiederfinden. Wenn du magst, melde dich gern direkt, damit wir es genauer nachzeichnen können, und komm zu einem anderen Zeitpunkt noch einmal vorbei. Dein Eindruck hilft uns, die Details zu schärfen, danke dir.

placeAddress: 136 Berlin Restaurant, Linienstraße 136, 10115 Berlin, Germany
text:
We ate at 136 for the first time last week and were absolutely delighted and impressed.

The food is characterized by beautiful presentation and deliciously intense flavors. Some of the little works of art were almost too beautiful to eat.

The restaurant also impresses with its superb service and its concept of showcasing the ingredients.

A particular highlight for me was the truly exceptional and interesting non-alcoholic pairing. I've rarely enjoyed it as much anywhere else.

We will definitely be back; the menu changes regularly, and we look forward to our next culinary experience at 136!
originalText:
Wir haben im 136 letzte Woche das erste Mal gegessen und waren sehr begeistert und beeindruckt.
Das Essen zeichnet sich aus durch wunderschöne Präsentation und köstlich-intensive Geschmackserlebnisse. Die kleinen Kunstwerke waren teilweise fast zu schade zum Aufessen.
Außerdem besticht das Restaurant durch den super Service und sein Konzept mit Präsentation der Zutaten.

The combination of Peruvian, Italian, and international influences is truly wonderful and unique. For almost every course, some ingredients are presented in small bowls at the table, as some of them aren't exactly everyday fare (at least not in Germany). placeAddress: 136 Berlin Restaurant, Linienstraße 136, 10115 Berlin, Germany
text:
Hello dear readers! Berlin, February 7, 2026

I was in the mood for a culinary treat, and unsurprisingly, Restaurant 136 with its top chef Mathiaz Díaz immediately came to mind. What I particularly appreciate about this restaurant is that the focus is primarily on the food – and not too much on the decor, which is rather rustic but cozy, or on other frills.

Together with friends, we opted for the seven-course menu with wine pairings. This time we were in luck: The wine pairings came from the Lungarotti winery in Umbria, known for its Montefalco Sagrantino wines, and were perfectly matched to each dish by the external manager, Francesco Zaganelli.

I don't want to go into detail about each individual dish this time, but rather summarize:

What a wonderful evening! Mathiaz Díaz is a chef brimming with creativity, yet—inexplicably—he has yet to receive Michelin stars. We are always surprised and delighted when his culinary creations melt on the tongue and the myriad flavors enchant our senses. He consistently manages to combine diverse ingredients into a stunning work of art. In art terms, one might say that an artist's quality is characterized by a high degree of recognizability—and this certainly applies to him.

The wine pairings were also exceptional: subtly nuanced and perfectly matched to each dish. The service was discreet and professional—always present, but never intrusive. I was particularly impressed by the selection of artfully arranged plates, the matching glasses for the wines, and the varied cutlery, which exuded a striking sense of luxury.

A heartfelt thank you for another unforgettable evening with the unmistakable signature of the "maître cuisinier."

We are already looking forward to our next visit…

Hallo liebe Leserschaft! Berlin, 07.02.26

Ich hatte mal wieder Lust auf eine kulinarische Verwöhnung, und wem wundert’s, da fiel mir das Restaurant 136 mit ihrem Spitzenkoch Mathiaz Díaz ein. Was ich an diesem Restaurant besonders schätze, ist, dass sich die Aufmerksamkeit des Gastes vorwiegend aufs Essen richtet – und nicht zu sehr auf die Einrichtung, die eher rustikal, aber gemütlich ausfällt, oder auf sonstigen Schnickschnack.
Gemeinsam mit Freunden entschieden wir uns für das Sieben-Gang-Menü mit Weinbegleitung. Dieses Mal hatten wir Glück: Die Weinbegleitung stammte vom Weingut Lungarotti in Umbrien, bekannt für seine Montefalco Sagrantino-Weine, und wurde vom externen Geschäftsführer Francesco Zaganelli perfekt auf jedes Gericht abgestimmt.
Ich möchte dieses Mal nicht auf jedes einzelne Gericht eingehen, sondern zusammenfassen:
Was für ein wundervoller Abend!  Mathiaz Díaz ist ein Koch, der vor Kreativität strotzt, dem aber – aus unerklärlicher Weise – die Sterne der Kochkunst noch verwehrt bleiben. Wir sind jedes Mal überrascht und begeistert, wenn seine „Genussentwürfe“ auf der Zunge zergehen und die vielfältigen Geschmacksnuancen unsere Sinne verzaubern. Er schafft es immer wieder, unterschiedlichste Produkte eindrucksvoll zu einem Gesamtkunstwerk zu inszenieren. In der Kunst würde man sagen: Die Qualität eines Künstlers zeigt sich durch einen hohen Wiedererkennungswert – und das trifft auf ihn wahrlich zu.
Auch die Weinbegleitung war außergewöhnlich: fein nuanciert auf jedes Gericht abgestimmt. Der Service war dezent und professionell – stets präsent, aber nie aufdringlich. Besonders beeindruckend fand ich die Auswahl der kunstvollen Teller, die passenden Gläser zur Weinbegleitung und das wechselnde Besteck, das in seiner Vielfalt auffällig luxuriös wirkte.
Ein herzlicher Dank für einen wieder unvergesslichen Abend mit der unverwechselbaren Handschrift des « maître cuisinier ».

text:
An Evening That Truly Impressed

I had requested a table for one at short notice – although Restaurant 136 was fully booked, they made it possible for me to get a table. I found this to be very accommodating and appreciated.

Something special has been created here: a unique, very well-thought-out fusion of Peruvian and Italian cuisine. For me, this is exactly how to elevate the artisanal tradition of Italian cuisine to a level that can easily compete with top-tier restaurants. The combination with the products, aromas, and spices of Peru is exceptionally successful and impressive.

I would particularly like to commend the chef, Matias Diaz, who takes very personal care of his guests. You can tell that it is truly important to him that the guest is comfortable. This attention and presence are rare these days and create a very positive impression.

The service was warm, attentive, and ran like clockwork. The wine pairings were also exciting, innovative, and fairly priced.

Ein Abend, der wirklich beeindruckt

Der Service war herzlich, aufmerksam und lief wie am Schnürchen. Auch die Weinbegleitung war spannend, innovativ und dabei fair kalkuliert.

Ein herzliches Dankeschön an Matias Diaz und das gesamte Team für diesen besonderen Abend – kulinarisch wie menschlich ein Erlebnis, das in Erinnerung bleibt.

The visual representation of the dishes was also quite weak and the tastes were mediocre at best (especially compared to any other fine dining place we had previously tried). Almost all of the bites tasted similar (acidic - vinegary due to similar ingredients in the sauces). And yes waiting for 4 hours was crazy long…

text:
I had the pleasure and desire to dine at 136 three times during my stays in Berlin, and, even though I was alone, I never felt truly alone or out of place.
The restaurant is small but comfortable, surrounded by an atmosphere of soft lighting and candlelight. Nicola, a young Italian sommelier, welcomes you with a smile and takes care to professionally recommend a good glass of wine to accompany your dinner.
The kitchen is open to the public, so during dinner you can watch the entire staff create small works of art on your plate.
Matias's art is like a symphonic composition where each ingredient is a unique entity in itself, but when combined with others, a dish is created that becomes a tasteful embrace on the palate.
I closed my eyes while savoring everything and experienced a true sensory journey; I can't describe it in any other words.
The 136 has become my favorite place and I have no other words to conclude this review than "Thank you and see you soon guys"!

Ho avuto il piacere e la volontà di cenare al 136 tre volte durante i miei soggiorni a Berlino, e, anche se in solitaria, ma non mi sono mai sentita veramente da sola o fuori luogo.

Ho chiuso gli occhi mentre gustavo il tutto ed ho vissuto un vero viaggio sensoriale, non saprei descriverlo con altre parole.
Il 136 è diventato il mio posto del cuore e non ho altre parole , per concludere questa recensione, che non siano “Grazie e a presto ragazzi”!

Das Essen war hervorragend - die Aromen waren perfekt aufeinander abgestimmt und die interessante Integration peruanischer Einflüsse machte jedes Gericht zu einem besonderen Geschmackserlebnis. Besonders beeindruckend war auch die schöne Präsentation der Speisen auf den Tellern. Ein absolutes Highlight waren die Involtini! Allein dieses Gericht ist einen Besuch wert.

Auch der Service verdient höchstes Lob: Das Personal war durchweg freundlich, aufmerksam und zuvorkommend. Die Atmosphäre im Restaurant ist sehr angenehm und lädt zum Verweilen ein. Man fühlt sich vom ersten Moment an willkommen und gut aufgehoben.

Das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis ist hervorragend. Eine klare Empfehlung für alle, die Wert auf außergewöhnliche Küche und erstklassigen Service legen. Ich komme auf jeden Fall wieder!

text:
We enjoyed the food, especially the risotto and chicken courses, although the chef tended to favor sour notes. We found it amusing when the waitress explained the “Brotzeit” first course, as if it was an avant-garde concept rather than the near ubiquitous (and sort of miserly) German practice of eating dark bread and cheese and butter for dinner.

The drinks program operated according to an idiosyncratic, and entrepreneurial, philosophy. The wine binder was as thick and impenetrable as a Dostoyevsky manuscript. Not that we had the time to look at it, as our waiter just barked things like “German or French!” “Dry?” “Are you ok with something a bit funky?” And ended up bringing us expensive bottles without ever indicating what the broader options were or what the price of anything was. This felt deliberate, given that the food waiter explained the chicken in so much detail that we practically knew its birth and death dates. The cherry on top came when my friend ordered a digestif. The drinks waiter barked “Fruit or herb?!” “Sweet or bitter!?” The bill revealed that the drinks waiter had lovingly selected an €80 digestif for our friend—roughly 2/3 of the price of the entire tasting menu—without ever mentioning the price.

My verdict: go if you can put it on your expense account. And order your drinks like you’re buying a used car.

placeDescription: Elevated locale for innovative, high-end 10-course meals made only from local ingredients.
text:
We went to Nobelhart & Schmutzig because the concept genuinely appealed to us. The idea of a restaurant built entirely around local and seasonal ingredients, served in a unique setting around a large open counter, sounded refreshing and original. We had also read quite a few negative reviews beforehand, but honestly assumed they were probably exaggerated. Unfortunately, after experiencing it ourselves, we can only conclude that most of those criticisms were entirely justified.

To start with the positive: the staff were genuinely friendly and spoke enthusiastically about the dishes and ingredients throughout the evening. Unfortunately, that is also where the positives largely ended for us.

The restaurant charges €140 for what is advertised as a “6-course menu”, which honestly feels misleading. The sixth “course” turns out to be a small sweet amuse handed to you at the door when you leave. In reality, you are paying €140 for 5 courses. At this price point, that simply feels cheap and slightly dishonest.

On top of that, we were back outside again within two hours. Partly because the pace of the evening is quite high, but also because the menu simply ends very quickly. There is very little sense of progression or rhythm, making the experience feel more like a short sequence of small plates than a proper fine dining experience.

The biggest disappointment, however, was the food itself. Not a single dish had any wow-factor. Nothing felt memorable, technically impressive, or surprising. We have eaten at several Michelin-starred restaurants before, and those experiences usually involve chefs truly transforming ingredients into something creative and unexpected. Here, almost everything leaned toward the boring side.

The vegetarian menu in particular was painfully disappointing for this price. The “main course” consisted of green asparagus with saffron sauce. That was it. No exciting technique, no creativity, no finesse — just asparagus on a plate. Serving that as a main course within a 5-course tasting menu is beneath any self-respecting restaurant.

We genuinely appreciate the philosophy around local and seasonal ingredients, but a good story alone is not enough. In the end, guests are paying for exceptional cooking, not for a manifesto about local produce. Too often, this felt like ingredients being placed on a plate without anything interesting actually being done with them.

Another striking detail is the strict no-photo policy. After this experience, we honestly understand very well why that policy exists.

What we found most unbelievable in the end is the Michelin star itself. In our opinion, it is completely undeserved. There are countless restaurants that combine sustainability, locality, and storytelling with genuinely exceptional food. Nobelhart & Schmutzig feels far more in love with its own concept than with delivering an outstanding dining experience.

Our advice: save yourself the disappointment and book one of the many far better alternatives Berlin has to offer.

text:
I wrote this review 5 years ago. This year, the restaurant hired a lawyer and forced google to remove negative reviews. If you scroll down, you will find that several people state the same thing and reposted their original review.

As other people already mentioned in their

This is a copy of my original Review from 2019:

“First of all, regarding the food, I don’t want to say that much. It is definitely not good but they state that their policy of only using local products would be worth the suboptimal taste. Not much you can do if you limit yourself to not using pepper, olive oil etc... We unfortunately did not know that before, but that’s our fault and if someone enjoys these self-imposed restrictions for some reason, they might find the taste interesting.

Regarding the experience, the first time we felt uncomfortable was when the owner of the place started to make inappropriate sexist comments. For example did the guest next to us ask him, why all waiters would wear a beard, to which he replied (quote) “as I like my men with moustaches and my women shaved”. He did that in a voice that was audible throughout the whole place and made us very uncomfortable. Again - if you are looking for this kind of entertainment, you might enjoy this.

After dinner we asked for the bill and were surprised as they charged us 60€ more than advertised on out menu. Asking for the reason we were told that out menu was the english one and had a wrong price for that date. On Thursdays they would always charge more and we could read that up online and got an email with the correct prize. After I showed them the email I received, which did not state any price, the owner got aggressive and hammered with his fist on the table (in front of all guests) and told us we could read it the correct price outside and what is written on the menu is only valid Mon-Wed, but if we insist, he would give us a discount.

My friend (chinese) asked him to stop shouting and using his fist as she felt very threatened by him, to which he replied this was a cultural problem she would not understand and should get used to, if she wants to live in the west.

We paid about 500€ and a whole evening for being insulted and threatened. The fact that we did not like the food is probably only secondary important and, as stated above, our own fault, as we did not inform ourselves about the ingredient-restrictions, which make a decent dish almost impossible.

I wrote an email afterwards to the restaurant, asking for a statement and did not get any reply.”

text:
While on a trip with my mum and wife, I wanted to take them somewhere special and treat my family to a memorable meal. I chose Nobelhart & Schmutzig as it is a very high-end restaurant, and we spent over £600 in total.

The meal itself was incredible. The food was genuinely some of the best we have tasted, and all three of us thoroughly enjoyed the experience from a culinary perspective. Up until the end of the evening, it felt like a fantastic choice and exactly the kind of special meal I had hoped to share with my family.

Unfortunately, the experience was soured at the end of the meal by the way tipping was handled. The lady serving us, who had a short blonde bob, put considerable pressure on us to leave a tip. I would like to be clear that I generally do tip when eating at restaurants, especially when the service and food are good. However, being asked so directly and in the manner it was delivered immediately made us feel uncomfortable.

What had been a very positive and memorable evening quickly became awkward and unpleasant. As we were leaving, the interaction made us feel pressured and uncomfortable, which was a real shame given how much we had enjoyed the food itself.

For a restaurant at this level, where guests are spending upwards of £200 per person, I would expect the service to be polished, discreet and professional throughout the full experience. Instead, the pressure around tipping left a negative final impression and overshadowed what should have been a brilliant evening.

Because of this, I will not be returning to the restaurant. I will also be sharing this feedback on the restaurant’s website, Google Reviews and TripAdvisor. While the food was excellent, I would warn others that they may feel put under considerable pressure to leave a tip at the end of the meal, which can really damage the overall experience.
ownerResponseText:
Hello Philip Hoy, 

Thank you very much for your email and for taking the time to write to us. 

Thank you for going to the trouble of sending us such a detailed account of your experience. 

In Germany, tipping is unfortunately part and parcel of dining out. At the same time, nobody is obliged to tip. Tips help to subsidise the prices of food and drink in the hospitality industry. It’s similar at the hairdresser’s, in taxis, at the massage parlour or at the beautician’s. Even though I’d like to change this, I have to adapt to the market. 

We wrote an article on this last year that explains the dilemma. https://nobelhartundschmutzig.com/en/tipping-reality-and-dilemma/

As tipping is part of the deal, credit card payment providers such as Nexi Europe have added a tipping function to their devices so that you can easily add a tip. This function appears after you have entered the total amount. 

Before the pandemic, as many as 10 percent of guests still paid in cash. Today, that figure is down to just 4 per cent. Consequently, almost no one carries cash anymore and has no opportunity to tip. This solution is therefore practical for both sides: the guest wants to tip because they were satisfied with the service, whilst the staff member also receives their tip. We divide the tips fairly among all staff members based on the hours they have worked.

At Nobelhart & Schmutzig, some of our guests come from different cultural backgrounds, so we feel the best approach is to enter the total amount and then explain the function to the guests. We say:‘The system will ask you for a tip. You have the option to leave one here. If you weren’t satisfied with your meal, you are of course under no obligation to leave a tip. If you were satisfied, you can now enter the amount you wish to tip.’ According to the staff member’s recollection, that is exactly what she did. At the same time, I would like to point out a possible language barrier.

I would like to apologise for the situation that arose; at the same time, on behalf of the Nobelhart & Schmutzig team, I would like to point out that we did not intend to pressure you into leaving a tip. 

Kind regards, Billy Wagner

The pace of service varied considerably—in the end, all tables were served at roughly the same time despite different start times, resulting in some people waiting a very long time and others feeling quite stressed. The ambiance was rather uninviting, and the restrooms were comparable to a regular coffee shop—unthinkable for a restaurant of this caliber. An iPad alarm clock also went off every few minutes in the open kitchen. The fact that we and the other guests were unceremoniously ushered out at exactly 11 with cream puffs immediately overshadowed the predominantly positive experience from before, especially since they're officially open until 12. Beware of the price trap with the wine pairing – you can find plenty of information about this online. Unfortunately, it didn't feel like a political statement or a thoughtful, forward-thinking approach. According to the restaurant, one dish (celeriac with nuts) was simply "stolen" by a cook who had worked there previously.

The concept of no cell phones at the table is great, but when you look at the food being presented, there's a good reason why cameras aren't allowed.

There were four of us, and we had a very enjoyable evening. The restaurant has an unusual design and a rather dark atmosphere. The focus is clearly on the open kitchen, around which a bar with most of the seating is located. You're right in the thick of things, which makes for a very lively evening. However, the stools were a bit uncomfortable for me during a stay of several hours.

Because of the bar-like setting, the service is very direct, as it's served from the kitchen area, just like at a bar. We liked this because it allowed for constant interaction. The team was consistently extremely friendly, attentive, and courteous, explaining everything clearly and patiently answering our questions.

The cuisine is more rustic than refined, but technically excellent and very creative. We had six courses, all of which were outstanding. You can clearly see that the cooking here is holistic and strongly influenced by regional ingredients. For someone like me, who doesn't eat everything, this was quite a challenge, but the execution was superb. The liver dumplings and the mustard egg were particularly memorable. In general, you'll leave more than satisfied; there's plenty of bread, and they even offered seconds after one course.

Personally, the wine pairing didn't quite appeal to me. Here, too, the restaurant follows a clear concept with wines from higher altitudes and more traditional, artisanal production methods, which tend to mean lighter wines. This isn't entirely to my taste and, in my opinion, didn't always pair perfectly with every course. However, the selection was certainly creative and interesting.

It's worth noting that this is a very concept-driven restaurant with a strong regional identity. It's certainly not for everyone, but given the quality offered and the very fair price, it's definitely worth a try.

text:
Initially, everything seemed quite promising.

The ban on cell phones is a bit odd – because you naturally want to document your experience... but it's possible to do without them sometimes...

The bottom line: just because you know the butter's birthday, the cow's name, and that the suppliers have a personal connection to the team, doesn't make it worth a star!

The quality is impeccable and the ideas are good and down-to-earth – but that's about it.

The service is, as expected, very good, sufficiently warm, and absolutely professional. I appreciate that you don't always need tweezers and floral designs to appear original and extravagant, but then you need something in the kitchen to stand out from very good cuisine.

The concept of regionality alone isn't enough for me to earn a star.

A lovely evening with very good food and friendly people! ... but nothing SPECIAL....

I would gladly share photos, but as I said, that's not allowed.

text: Billy Wagner is not merely a restaurant owner, nor simply a sommelier—he is a visionary of modern German food culture. His ideals of sustainability, devotion to locally sourced ingredients, and commitment to impassioned slow-farming practices culminate in a dining experience found nowhere else in the world: Nobelhart & Schmutzig. At this Berlin-based restaurant, one doesn't find the typical surgically precise, Michelin-style cooking. Rather, together with music playing on vinyl and ongoing interactions with "the cast," it is a house of devotion to the simplest, most essential and profound things in life: the food that sustains us, and the shared act of eating and drinking that makes us feel truly alive. Dining here connects you to place—to the German terroir and emotional landscape of Berlin. The wine list is not a tomb but a collection of bottles disclosing Wagner’s relationships with regional winemakers. Modern German winemaking, much like local slow farming, is rooted in a profound love of land and life—driven by respect for the earth and the vitality it gives back. Every bottle tells a story of place, patience, and purpose. To eat here is to participate in a living movement. Together with his team—especially the wonderful Greta and Martyna—Wagner invites guests to taste, enjoy, and truly digest a meaningful expression of modern Germany. If you are lucky, you may carry a piece of it away in your heart. At the very least, you will leave with the signature parting dessert.

We were there last Friday.

We had a reservation. We then waited for 40 minutes without the young waitress acknowledging us or any of the other guests. We finally got their attention and were able to order drinks and food after almost 45 minutes.

If we hadn't said anything, who knows when someone would have come.

Behind us was a loud group of men who addressed the waiters by name and were constantly served, while we still hadn't received our drinks after almost an hour. You couldn't call that a pleasant atmosphere. It would be nice if the waiters would say something, since they were hanging around chatting with those loud men the whole time and disturbing all the other guests.

And you could see that the other guests around us were also annoyed.

We've been here many times before, always before visiting the Friedrichstadt-Palast, which is directly across the street, but we probably won't be coming back now. What a shame.

The food was quite tasty, at least, and the portions were large.

placeAddress: Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer, Unter den Linden 77, 10117 Berlin, Germany
placeDescription: Elegant restaurant with creative cuisine, as well as views of the Brandenburg Gate.
text:
Lorenz Adlon Essimer, a two-Michelin-star fine dining restaurant located in the heart of Berlin overlooking the Brandenburg Gate, embraces influences and ideas from across Europe while actively incorporating Asian sensibilities into its modern fine dining.

The flavors and textures harmonize across the 6, 7, and 8-course tasting menus, featuring dishes such as sea bass with chicory, kohlrabi, and orange, and wild turbot with grapefruit, celery, and hazelnut. Duck liver, its various variations, and sour cream also showcase the kitchen's confident craftsmanship.

The restaurant's elegant wood-paneled dining room exudes class and the luxury of the classic world, reflecting Adlon's rich history. Past guests include Thomas Edison, Henry Ford, and John D. Rockefeller.

6, 7, 8코스 시식 메뉴에 걸친 맛과 식감이 어우러져 치커리, 콜라비, 오렌지가 들어간 농어, 자몽, 셀러리, 헤이즐넛이 들어간 야생 터벗 같은 요리가 어우러집니다. 오리 간과 다양한 변형과 사워크림도 주방에서 자신감 넘치는 솜씨를 보여줍니다.

text: Tired of the same old Michelin one-star dinners, but the prices of three-star restaurants are prohibitive? If that's your thought, then a two-Michelin-starred restaurant is an excellent option. But how do you choose the right two-Michelin-starred restaurant for a perfect evening? After all, we don't want a perfect evening ruined by the wrong restaurant. If you share this dilemma and are planning a trip to Berlin, then let me introduce you to Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer. Located in the prestigious Adlon Kempinski Hotel, right next to the Brandenburg Gate, a famous Berlin landmark, this restaurant offers the chance to enjoy a delicious dinner while gazing at the magnificent gate. As I mentioned before, a perfect restaurant should excel in four aspects: ambiance, taste, service, and ingredients. Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer delivers on all four. Its retro European-style decor will make you feel like you've stepped into an 18th-century royal dining room. You might initially worry that you've chosen the wrong restaurant and ruined a perfect evening. The exceptional service here will surely put your mind at ease. If you're worried about the food, rest assured, one bite of the delicious lamb will prove all your concerns unfounded. Of course, you'll only truly understand this when you're actually seated in Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer's perfect restaurant and savor a delicious lamb. If you're looking for a perfect evening, whether alone or with your loved ones, friends, or family, Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer is the perfect choice.

text:
Following the change in the kitchen, we finally made it to the dining room. Having already dined at what felt like every Michelin-starred restaurant in the capital, and having followed J. Zörner for quite some time, the Adlon was finally on our list.

Although we initially had some doubts about the dining room's supposedly dated style, we were pleasantly surprised throughout.

The menu was outstanding. We wish the chef and his young team the best of luck in taking the next logical step.

I would particularly like to commend the service. Confident and professional, yet always very friendly and humorous. The sophisticated conversations with the restaurant manager and sommelier will be remembered for a long time and are a true benchmark for Michelin-starred service.

Many thanks and see you soon.

AF MF PG
originalText:
Im Zuge des Wechsels am Herd, trieb es uns nun endlich auch mal ins Esszimmer. Nachdem wir ansonsten gefühlt jede Sterne-Station in der Hauptstadt durch hatten, und J Zörner ohnehin schon lange begleiten, war das Adlon nun endlich fällig.

Obwohl unsererseits anfänglich durchaus etwas Zweifel am vermeintlich angestaubten Stil des Esszimmers haftete, wurden wir -durchweg- positiv überrascht.

Das Menü war herausragend gut. Wir drücken die Daumen, dass der Küchenchef und sein junges Team hier den nächsten logischen Schritt machen können.

Besonders möchte ich den Service loben. Souverän und professionell, aber stets sehr sympathisch und humorvoll. Die niveauvollen Schwätzchen mit Restaurantleitung und Sommelier werden lange in Erinnerung bleiben und sind eine echte Benchmark was Sterne-Service betrifft.

Herzlichen Dank und bis bald.

AF MF PG

text:
Fine Dining of a Special Kind

I recently visited Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer with my girlfriend to enjoy a six-course meal. A restaurant in this price range is, of course, very exclusive. Five of the six tables were occupied, the lighting was pleasantly dimmed, and the atmosphere was relaxed and stylish.

The diverse dishes were served one after the other, and each course was accompanied by a small presentation explaining its preparation and origin. The courses were paired with carefully selected wines, which not only complemented the food perfectly but also noticeably contributed to the lively atmosphere of the evening from the middle of the meal onward. The staff was attentive, friendly, and courteous without seeming pretentious.

For me, this kind of experience is definitely not for everyday dining – I'm more of a simple burger kind of guy. But if you want to treat yourself and enjoy the finest dishes with exclusive service in an upscale setting, this is the place to be.
originalText:
Fine Dining der besonderen Art

Ich war vor einiger Zeit mit meiner Freundin im Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer, um ein 6-Gänge-Menü zu genießen. Ein Restaurant in dieser Preiskategorie ist natürlich sehr exklusiv gehalten. Insgesamt waren fünf der sechs Tische besetzt, die Beleuchtung war angenehm gedimmt, und es herrschte eine entspannte, stilvolle Atmosphäre.

Die verschiedensten Speisen wurden nacheinander serviert, und zu jeder Speise gab es eine kleine Präsentation mit Informationen zur Zubereitung und Herkunft. Begleitet wurden die Gänge von ausgewählten Weinsorten, welche nicht nur gut zum Essen gepasst haben, sondern ab der Mitte des Menüs auch merklich zur ausgelassenen Stimmung des Abends beitgetragen haben. Das Personal war engagiert, freundlich und zuvorkommend, ohne dabei aufgesetzt zu wirken.

Für mich ist so ein Erlebnis definitiv nichts für den Alltag – da bin ich doch eher ein einfacher Burgertyp. Aber wenn man sich mal etwas gönnen möchte und in gehobenem Ambiente die feinsten Gerichte mit exklusivem Service genießen will, ist man hier bestens aufgehoben.

Amrit Restaurant is fantastic.

The staff was incredibly friendly, especially Dhillon, our waiter. He was incredibly attentive, courteous, and always there when we needed anything. He was also so warm and welcoming. The food was also delicious. I highly recommend the butter chicken. Overall, a top-notch restaurant with great service and superb food. We'll definitely be back!

placeDescription: Elegant restaurant with creative cuisine, as well as views of the Brandenburg Gate.
text:
We sat in the library, which boasts a beautiful historical ambiance and a view of the Brandenburg Gate. We received a very warm welcome and excellent service, and enjoyed a truly impeccable six-course menu with wine pairings.

Each course was not only visually and technically perfect, but each one also tasted so delicious that I couldn't have imagined skipping it.

Mr. Konrad's wine pairings were wonderful, and for a Berlin restaurant, the value for money was excellent. Wonderful, classic wines were served, thankfully avoiding trendy styles and regions.

The service was also very pleasant and, despite the formal setting, not at all stiff. It was a real treat that both the service manager, Oliver Kraft, and the owner himself, Reto Brändli, took the time to speak with us – surprisingly personal! Thank you so much!

We're already looking forward to seeing the team again at the kitchen party!

All in all, this is probably one of the most stylish restaurants in Berlin where you can enjoy excellent food and drinks and truly relax. Of course: naturally at a price commensurate with the effort involved.
originalText:
Wir saßen in der Bibliothek mit einem schönen historischen Ambiente und Blick auf das Brandenburger Tor, wurden sehr freundlich begrüßt und bedient und hatten ein wirklich makelloses 6-Gang Menü mit Weinbegleitung.

Jeder Gang war nicht nur visuell und handwerklich perfekt umgesetzt, auch hat  wirklich jeder Gang so gut geschmeckt, dass ich nicht gewusst hätte welchen Gang ich ggf auslassen würde.

Die Weinbegleitung von Hr.Konrad war wunderbar und für Berliner Restaurants stimmte hier auch die Preis Leistung, es wurden wunderbare, klassische Weine serviert und zum Glück auf trendige Weinstile und Regionen verzichtet.

Auch der Service war sehr angenehm und trotz des formellen Ambiente nicht steif. Dass sich sowohl Serviceleiter Oliver Kraft als auch der Chef persönlich, Reto Brändli, sich Zeit für uns genommen haben war höchst angenehm und sogar überraschend persönlich, vielen Dank!
Wir freuen uns schon das Team auf der Küchenparty wieder zu treffen!

placeAddress: SOY, Rosa-Luxemburg-Straße 30, 10178 Berlin, Germany
placeDescription: Plant-based Vietnamese food, with noodles & curries, in a modern, airy space with outdoor seats.
text:
This was my favorite restaurant for the past five years, but sadly, it's no longer my favorite.

I ate here today with a friend. The menu is definitely not as extensive or as good as it used to be. There are far fewer dishes than before.

We ordered the same dish and asked for our leftovers (which were almost a full plate) to be packed together in a box.

However, we only received a small box that was at most half full. What was previously on the plate was barely a third of what was left, even with a generous interpretation. It makes no sense to throw away most of the food that's already been paid for and only give the paying customer a small portion.

So, SOY has unfortunately lost its place as my favorite restaurant.

The decor has also deteriorated. It used to look much nicer.

Update:

I see that the owner only responded to my review with "🧢". That's slang for expecting me to lie. Because of this reaction, I'm reducing my rating from 2 to 1 star.

I had at least expected a respectful and understanding response. Instead, being indirectly portrayed as a liar after expressing my disappointment with my visit is deeply disappointing and unacceptable. This is especially bitter for me because this restaurant was my favorite for many years, and I told everyone how good it was.
originalText:
War jetzt für 5 Jahre mein lieblings Restaurant jetzt leider nicht mehr.

Ich war heute zu zweit hier essen. Die Karte ist definitiv nicht mehr so groß und gut wie sie zuvor war. Viel weniger Gerichte als damals.

Wir haben das gleiche Gericht gegessen und haben am Ende unsere Reste (die schon fast ein voller Teller waren) zusammen in eine box einpacken lassen.

Bekommen haben wir aber nur eine kleine box die maximal zur Hälfte gefüllt waren. Das was zuvor auf dem Teller war ist nur noch mit Augen zudrücken zu einem Drittel drin gewesen. Es macht keinen sinn dieses bereits bezahlte essen größtenteils wegzuwerfen und dem bezahlenden Kunden nur noch ein kleinen Teil zu geben.

Den Platz als Lieblings Restaurant hat das SOY somit leider verloren.

Es wurde auch die Dekoration verschlechtert. Früher sah es schöner aus.

Update:

Ich sehe, dass der Inhaber auf meine Bewertung lediglich mit "🧢“ geantwortet hat. Das ist ja slang dafür das ich lügen soll. Aufgrund dieser Reaktion reduziere ich meine Bewertung von 2 auf 1 Stern.

Ich hatte zumindest mit einer respektvollen und verständnisvollen Antwort gerechnet. Stattdessen indirekt als Lügner dargestellt zu werden, nachdem ich meine Enttäuschung über meinen Besuch geschildert habe, empfinde ich als sehr enttäuschend und inakzeptabel. Besonders bitter ist das für mich, da dieses Restaurant über viele Jahre hinweg mein Lieblingsrestaurant war und ich jedem darüber erzählt habe wie gut es ist.
ownerResponseText:
Yes, I responded with the 🧢.

Not because I wanted to attack you personally, but because the claim that we deliberately threw away a large portion of your already paid-for food is truly outrageous.

And to be honest, with this accusation, you've definitely secured a spot in our top three for "Cap of the Year." Not because we mind criticism of the menu or the decor—opinions on that are certainly subjective. But because the claim that we intentionally throw away our guests' food is both absurd and damaging to our reputation.

We don't stand for that sort of thing, neither as a restaurant nor as individuals.

After five years as your supposed favorite restaurant, we honestly expected fair criticism rather than such accusations.
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Ja, ich habe mit dem 🧢 geantwortet.

Nicht, weil ich Sie persönlich angreifen wollte, sondern weil die Behauptung, wir hätten einen Großteil Ihres bereits bezahlten Essens absichtlich weggeworfen, wirklich wild ist.

Und ich will ehrlich sein: Mit dieser Unterstellung haben Sie sich auf jeden Fall einen Platz in unseren Top 3 für den „Cap des Jahres“ gesichert. Nicht, weil uns Kritik an der Karte oder der Deko stört, darüber kann man unterschiedlicher Meinung sein. Sondern weil die Behauptung, wir würden absichtlich Essen unserer Gäste wegschmeißen, gleichzeitig absurd und rufschädigend ist.

Für so etwas stehen wir weder als Restaurant noch als Menschen. 

Nach fünf Jahren als angebliches Lieblingsrestaurant hätten wir ehrlich gesagt eher mit fairer Kritik gerechnet als mit derartigen Unterstellungen.

text:
A very cozy, casual restaurant, perfect for a solo visit. The atmosphere is relaxed, the clientele is mixed, and you immediately feel at ease.

The service was exceptionally friendly, attentive, helpful, and quick on both visits. In my opinion, the price-performance ratio is absolutely reasonable for the quality and the portion sizes.

The food: excellent and filling.

I went there twice and each time had the cucumber salad (see picture), as well as dish #40 on the first visit and #41 on the second. All dishes were very well prepared, fresh, and delicious.

I personally enjoy spicy food.

The cucumber salad was perfectly seasoned and had an ideal, pleasant level of spiciness for me. The main course, although labeled as spicy, could have used a bit more spice for my taste. On my second visit, I simply asked for more spice – no problem at all, and they added fresh chili. That's exactly the kind of service you want.

I went there for lunch both times and had no trouble getting a table without a reservation.

The location right next to the Babylon cinema is a big plus. I can wholeheartedly recommend SOY Berlin and will definitely come back.

The restaurant is on the pricier side. For the quality of the food, I felt the price-performance ratio was a bit too high.

On the other hand, the beer was very tasty and served at the perfect temperature.

Overall, a solid restaurant with very good service, but I had expected significantly more from the food.

Best regards,
Möller Hospitality Audit

The good and the bad.

The good: the food was well-prepared, but even though we're not big eaters, we didn't eat very much.

The bad: the welcome wasn't very warm, even though they made an effort for those who don't speak German.

Overal with this amount one can still find much better food in Berlin and in a better location.

text:
We went for a meal as a couple.
- Regarding food quality: I ordered sugarcane juice but it was spoiled. I called a staff member, and they said they wanted a change, but I didn't receive an apology. I switched to tamarind iced tea, but it was incredibly sweet. I ordered 5 dishes: fried fermented pork rolls were all batter (5/10), grilled chicken feet were decent (9/10), grilled oysters with scallion oil (7/10), snails with salted egg sauce (6/10 because they were salty and lacked the aroma of the sauce), and the blood cockles with garlic were "rotten." I called a staff member again, but they just took the plate away.

- After complaining twice about the service quality, I received no response from the restaurant, not even a staff member came to ask about the quality of the food while I was eating.
The bill was €118.80. The restaurant is doing too much seeding!
originalText:
Mình đi ăn 2 người
- Về chất lượng đồ ăn : Mình đặt nước mía nhưng bị hỏng, gọi nhân viên ra thì bảo đổi nước nhưng cũng không hề nhận được 1 câu xin lỗi từ quán. Mình có đổi sang me đá thì thôi nó ngọt kinh khủng. Mình gọi 5 món, nem chua rán thì toàn bột 5/10, chân gà nướng ăn ổn 9/10, hàu nướng mỡ hành 7/10, ốc hương sốt trứng muối 6/10 vì mặn và không thấy mùi thơm của sốt, sò huyết cháy tỏi thì sò “ thối “ gọi tiếp nhân viên ra, nhưng cũng chỉ bê đĩa đồ ăn đi.
- Sau 2 lần phàn nàn về chất lượng dịch vụ thì mình không hề nhận được phản hồi của nhà hàng, ngay cả khi ăn cũng không được nhân viên ra hỏi về chất lượng.
Hoá đơn hết 118,80€ nie wieder. Quán chạy seeding quá nhiều ‼️‼️
ownerResponseText:
Thank you for taking the time to share your very detailed experience.

We are truly sorry to hear that your meal did not meet your expectations, especially regarding food quality and service.

The issues you raised, such as the drinks not meeting expectations, the food flavors not being to your liking, and the way the staff handled the situation, are points we take very seriously. We apologize for not receiving timely support and feedback during your meal.

We will forward all this feedback to management, the kitchen staff, and the service staff to review our procedures, retrain them, and improve service quality in the future.

We hope to have the opportunity to welcome you again so that we can provide a better experience.
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Cảm ơn bạn đã dành thời gian chia sẻ trải nghiệm rất chi tiết của mình.
Chúng tôi thực sự rất tiếc khi biết rằng bữa ăn của bạn không đáp ứng được kỳ vọng, đặc biệt là về chất lượng món ăn và trải nghiệm dịch vụ.

Những vấn đề bạn nêu như đồ uống không đạt chất lượng mong đợi, hương vị món ăn chưa phù hợp, cũng như cách xử lý tình huống của nhân viên là những điểm chúng tôi đặc biệt nghiêm túc ghi nhận. Chúng tôi xin lỗi vì bạn đã không nhận được sự hỗ trợ và phản hồi kịp thời trong lúc dùng bữa.

Chúng tôi sẽ chuyển toàn bộ phản hồi này đến quản lý và đội ngũ bếp cũng như nhân viên phục vụ để xem xét lại quy trình làm việc, đào tạo lại và cải thiện chất lượng phục vụ trong tương lai.

Rất mong có cơ hội được đón tiếp bạn nữa để chúng tôi có thể mang đến trải nghiệm tốt hơn.

text:
My first meal in Germany! I had the Für unsere kleinen: chicken schnitzel served in breadcrumbs baked with cranberry jelly and french fries.

The chicken breading was very delicious, but did not stick to the chicken and fell off immediately when I picked it up. The cranberry sauce that came with the chicken, was absolutely delicious. I really surprised at how good jelly on chicken was, which I guess is common in Germany. The fries were absolutely delicious, they tasted airy and soft. The taste seemed to melt within my mouth. The lemonade I ordered came out and was sprite with a hint of lemon. I was really surprised at first, but quickly realized that almost every drink in Germany is carbonated. This was a really great first meal and I am excited for more!

text:
Unfortunately, a huge disappointment. The food used to be significantly better, but it seems either the chef has changed or the recipes have been altered. The dishes were now very average and nowhere near the standard we were used to.

Even worse, however, was the service. The female server was extremely unfriendly and made us feel like we had to beg to even be allowed to eat there. Such an atmosphere in a restaurant of this price range is simply unacceptable. The male server was at least a bit friendlier, which made the evening slightly more pleasant.

In the end, we spent around €250, and with the tip, even €260. This is absolutely unjustified for the quality and service. Very disappointing – we definitely won't be coming back.
originalText:
Leider eine große Enttäuschung. Früher war das Essen hier deutlich besser, aber inzwischen scheint entweder der Koch gewechselt zu haben oder die Rezepte wurden verändert. Die Gerichte waren nur noch sehr durchschnittlich und überhaupt nicht mehr auf dem Niveau, das wir von früher kannten.

Noch schlimmer war allerdings der Service. Die weibliche Bedienung war extrem unfreundlich und hat uns das Gefühl gegeben, als müssten wir darum bitten, überhaupt dort essen zu dürfen. So eine Atmosphäre bei einem Restaurant dieser Preisklasse ist einfach unangemessen. Der männliche Servicekraft war wenigstens etwas freundlicher, was den Abend minimal angenehmer gemacht hat.

Am Ende haben wir rund 250 € ausgegeben, mit Trinkgeld sogar 260 €. Für diese Qualität und diesen Service ist das absolut nicht gerechtfertigt. Sehr enttäuschend – wir werden definitiv nicht wiederkommen.
ownerResponseText:

Ihre Rückmeldung zu den Gerichten nehmen wir sehr ernst. Wir verstehen, dass Veränderungen im Geschmack oder in der Wahrnehmung enttäuschend sein können, und werden dies intern mit unserem Küchenteam sorgfältig besprechen und prüfen.

Ebenso bedauern wir sehr, dass Sie den Service als unfreundlich empfunden haben. Freundlichkeit und Gastfreundschaft sind für uns zentrale Werte, und wir werden Ihr Feedback mit dem gesamten Team reflektieren und gezielt nacharbeiten.

ownerResponseText:
Thank you for taking the time to share your experience in detail.

We are delighted to read that you enjoyed the restaurant's ambiance, as well as our red curry and rice, and that you found the portions generous. This is very gratifying.

However, we are sincerely sorry to hear that the desserts did not meet your expectations, particularly in terms of taste and balance. Your feedback is valuable and will be passed on to our kitchen team so they can evaluate and improve these recipes.

We also regret the wait and the feeling you experienced regarding the service when ordering your desserts. This does not reflect the level of attention we strive to offer our guests, and we will discuss this with our team.

Thank you again for your feedback, which helps us improve. We hope to have the opportunity to offer you a completely satisfying experience on your next visit.
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Merci d’avoir pris le temps de partager votre expérience en détail.

Nous sommes ravis de lire que vous avez apprécié le cadre du restaurant, ainsi que notre curry rouge et le riz, et que vous avez trouvé les portions généreuses. Cela nous fait très plaisir.

Nous sommes en revanche sincèrement désolés d’apprendre que les desserts n’ont pas été à la hauteur de vos attentes, notamment en termes de goût et d’équilibre. Vos remarques sont précieuses et seront transmises à notre équipe de cuisine afin d’évaluer et d’améliorer ces recettes.

Nous regrettons également l’attente et le ressenti concernant le service lors de votre commande des desserts. Cela ne correspond pas au niveau d’attention que nous souhaitons offrir à nos clients, et nous allons en discuter avec notre équipe.

Merci encore pour votre retour, qui nous aide à progresser. Nous espérons avoir l’occasion de vous offrir une expérience entièrement satisfaisante lors d’une prochaine visite.

text:
The food was absolutely fantastic. It’s good value for money 64€ for a 5 course and 44€ for the wine pairing, are really reasonable with this outstanding quality of food.

It felt like a very German, straightforward fine dining experience. No bells and whistles, just outstanding ingredients, prepared to the point, with a little twist. Accompanying wine selection was on point as well. Our menu was a take on German and Austrian classics.

The atmosphere felt similarly simplistic German. We went for my wife’s birthday dinner and perhaps were hoping for a more cosy/ romantic experience. I could imagine the outside seating giving a different ambience, but inside downstairs for us wasn’t it. Of course this is something subjective and others will feel differently.

All in all we had a good time and liked the interpretations, but the atmosphere wasn’t for us. I would also recommend taking the 7 course 95€ menu, as I could have easily eaten more.

The place was alright. They seem to specialize in grilled food. I thought to myself: they can do currywurst. Even at 5:30 in the afternoon.

The sauce was good, but the sausage had clearly been sitting out for a while. As a grill master, I wouldn't have served it. Perhaps this doesn't happen as often when the place is busier later in the evening, but it was still a bit disappointing. Especially since the price seemed higher.

So, while we received very friendly service and left satisfied, next time I'll definitely check what's on the grill before I sit down.

text:
Overall, we had a lovely evening and opted for the seven-course menu with wine pairings. The atmosphere was pleasant, and the service was consistently friendly and attentive, though at times it felt a bit rushed.

Unfortunately, the food itself left us with mixed feelings. The dishes were well-prepared, but rather bland in flavor – they lacked the distinctive aromas or combinations that truly make a lasting impression. Furthermore, some courses were served lukewarm, and in some cases, even cold.

From the second half of the menu onward, there were longer pauses between courses, which disrupted the flow somewhat. We also would have appreciated more interesting textures in the individual dishes. While the presentation was decent, the food lacked that certain something that makes a menu in this price range stand out.

Overall, we had a pleasant evening, but given the points mentioned, we feel the value for money isn't quite right.
originalText:
Wir hatten insgesamt einen schönen Abend und haben uns für das 7-Gänge-Menü mit Weinbegleitung entschieden. Die Atmosphäre war angenehm und der Service durchweg freundlich und zuvorkommend, wirkte jedoch stellenweise etwas gehetzt.

Das Essen selbst hat bei uns leider gemischte Eindrücke hinterlassen. Die Gerichte waren solide zubereitet, wirkten geschmacklich jedoch eher nüchtern – es fehlten die besonderen Aromen oder Kombinationen, die wirklich in Erinnerung bleiben. Zudem wurden einzelne Gänge nur lauwarm bis teilweise sogar kalt serviert.

Ab der zweiten Hälfte des Menüs entstanden längere Pausen zwischen den Gängen, wodurch der Ablauf etwas ins Stocken geraten ist. Auch bei den einzelnen Gerichten hätten wir uns mehr spannende Texturen gewünscht. Optisch waren die Teller zwar ordentlich angerichtet, aber es fehlte das gewisse Extra, das ein Menü dieser Preisklasse besonders macht.

Insgesamt hatten wir einen angenehmen Abend, dennoch empfinden wir das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis angesichts der genannten Punkte als nicht ganz ausgewogen.

placeDescription: Creative European fare in a high-ceilinged old distillery with bare boards & tiles, plus a terrace.
text:
After the concept change, it's safe to say: it was worth it. The €60 net menu is more than fair. Excellent wine list. We had a Sauvignon Blanc from Styria. Fairly priced.

Lovely appetizers to start. Then:

Robill – a kind of carpaccio with honey and pine nuts. Very good.

Yellow beetroot – vegetables in a very, very good broth.

Venison dürüm – a superbly seasoned wrap. Top-quality meat, a highlight!

Sturgeon with beetroot – was indeed sturgeon with beetroot. Good. Perhaps it would have been better placed before the venison.

Elderflower, banana ice cream, pecan nut – although I hate bananas, this was a very, very good, harmonious dessert.

Good, attentive service; the ambiance is quite industrial.

Overall, a very pleasant evening with very reasonable prices, far removed from the now completely outlandish world of Michelin-starred restaurants. The cuisine is below Michelin stars, but very, very good. Definitely worth a visit.

Nach Umstellung des Konzeptes kann man sagen: Es hat sich gelohnt. Menü zu 60 € netto ist mehr als fair. Sehr gute Weinkarte. Wir hatten einen Sauvignon blanc aus der Steiermark. Fair bepreist.
Schöne Häppchen vorneweg. Dann:
Rinderrücken - eine Art Carpaccio mit Honig und Pinienkerne. Sehr gut
Gelbe Beete - Gemüse in sehr sehr guter Brühe.
Hirsch Dürüm - Ein super gewürzter Wrap. Top Fleisch, Highlight!
Stör mit Rote Beete - war Stör mit Rote Beete. Gut. Wäre vor dem Hirsch vielleicht besser positioniert.
Holunder, Bananeneis, Pekannuss - Obwohl ich Bananen hasse, war das ein sehr sehr gutes, stimmiges Dessert.
Guter, aufmerksamer Service, man sitzt ganz schön im Industrie-Ambiente.
Insgesamt ein sehr schöner Abend mit sehr abnehmbarem Preisniveau fernab der inzwischen völlig abgedrehten Sterne-Gastronomie. Küchenniveau unterhalb der Sterne, aber sehr sehr gut. Kann man öfter hingehen.

text:
As with a lot of places in Berlin the menu is limited, pork or chicken.........but what they do serve is excellent!
The interior of the restaurant in very dark with neon lights on the walls and taken up in the large portion by the cooking area. The waiter seated us straight away and gave us the menus. We were waiting for a couple more people to join us so he left us alone. When the order was taken the food was delivered quickly and was fantastic. We had the 9 crispy chicken wings, half a chicken and chips with extra white cabbage salad, a small rack of ribs with chips, loaded fries and a double curry worst with chips. placeDescription: Japanese yakiniku dining on marbled wagyu beef, grilled at the table in elegant wooden surroundings.
text:
I've been going here for many years and really enjoy it. The meat is of very good quality, and the simplicity of the dishes makes it a lot of fun! It's a very straightforward concept, which is a big advantage for the kitchen since most dishes are simply portioned and then prepared by the guest at the table grill. This certainly boosts the reviews. However, the first-class service deserves special mention. The only slight drawback is the price of some side dishes (a raw and unseasoned carrot or three finely chopped mushrooms for €5??!?).

And I've also been a bit annoyed with the Wagyu wild cut on a few occasions, as it's a matter of luck because it's essentially trimmings from different parts of the Wagyu. Sometimes they're good cuts, and other times I wish I'd ordered a bit more of a different cut.

Overall, though, you usually leave happy and satisfied, which is the least you should expect when the bill is at least €150 per person, not including wine or other alcoholic beverages.


And I've also had a few hiccups with the Wagyu wild cut, as it's essentially a matter of luck. I recommend coming in a group of four, as this gives you the opportunity to try many dishes since everything is perfect for sharing.

Larger groups will need to be split up, as only a maximum of four people fit at one table.
originalText:
Gehe hier schon seit vielen Jahren gerne hin. Sehr gute Qualität an Fleisch und wegen der Einfachheit der Gerichte macht es echt viel Spaß! Es ist ein sehr einfaches Konzept welches sehr von Vorteil für die Küche ist da die meisten Gerichte nur portioniert werden und dann vom Gast zubereitet werden am Tischgrill. Dies ist sicher sehr vorteilhaft für die Bewertungen. Allerdings muss man den erstklassigen Service positiv hervorheben. Lediglich die Preise für manche Beilagen könnte man ein klein wenig bemängeln ( eine rohe und ungewürzte Karotte/ oder 3 Champignons klein geschnitten für 5 Euro??!?)
Und auch bei dem wagyu wild cut habe ich mich schon das ein oder andere Mal etwas aufgeregt, da muss man Glück haben denn es sind quasi die Abschnitte von den verschiedenen wagyu Teilen. Manchmal sind es gute Abschnitte und manchmal hätte man dann doch lieber noch etwas mehr von einem anderen Teilstück bestellt.
Im großen und Ganzen geht man jedoch meist glücklich und zufrieden raus, was jedoch bei einer Rechnung von min 150 Euro pro Person ohne Wein oder alkoholischen Getränken auch das mindeste sein sollte.
Ich empfehle zu 4. zu kommen denn dann hat man die Möglichkeit viele Gerichte zu probieren da sich alles wunderbar zum teilen eignet.
Größere Gruppen müssen geteilt werden da nur max 4 Personen an einen Tisch passen.
