placeDescription: Japanese yakiniku dining on marbled wagyu beef, grilled at the table in elegant wooden surroundings.
text:
This is by far the best thing I've ever eaten.

I've eaten Kobe beef in Japan and at various yakiniku restaurants in Berlin, and it's become increasingly clear to me what a gem this restaurant is.

The meat is incredibly tender and cut to the perfect size and thickness. The sauces are by no means overpowering, but perfectly complement the meat. Although I'm usually against sauces/marinades with meat, I always eat it with sauce here, even though it's not strictly necessary. The special table grill doesn't add any coloring that I'm aware of, so you get to enjoy the pure Wagyu flavor. Even the vegetables somehow take on a special quality on the grill, though I can't quite put my finger on why.

Beyond the taste, the restaurant itself is an absolute experience. Subdued, pleasant lighting creates an elegant ambiance, and the ritual of placing the meat on the grill yourself, especially when dining as a group, fosters a sense of community. I've only ever had wonderful evenings here.

The staff is very friendly and always helpful.

The prices are absolutely fair for such a high-end establishment.

The only downside is that lately I've had trouble getting a table without booking several days in advance. You definitely need to book well in advance. But that speaks in favor of the restaurant, not against it.
originalText:
Bis hierhin das Beste was ich jemals gegessen habe.

Ich habe schon Kobe-Rind in Japan gegessen und verschiedene Yakiniku Restaurants in Berlin und mir ist immer klarer geworden was für ein Juwel dieses Restaurant ist.

Das Fleisch ist unfassbar zart, und in die perfekte Größe und Dicke geschnitten. Die Soßen sind keinesfalls zu dominant, aber runden das Fleisch perfekt ab. Obwohl ich bei Fleisch sonst gegen Soßen/Marinaden bin esse ich hier immer mit Soße auch wenn das natürlich nicht notwendig wäre. Der spezielle Tischgrill fügt keine mir bewusste Geschmacksfärbung hinzu, somit kommt man in den Genuss puren Wagyu-Geschmacks. Auch das Gemüse wird irgndwie besonders auf dem Grill ohne dass ich das erklären könnte.

Abseits vom Geschmack ist das Restaurant ein absolutes Erlebnis. Gedämpftes angenehmes Licht schaffen ein edles Ambiente und das Ritual das Fleisch selber aufzulegen führt, wenn man als Gruppe da ist, zu einer Gemeinschafts-Erfahrung. Ich hatte bis jetzt nur großartige Abende hier.

Das Personal ist sehr freundlich und immer hilfsbereit.
Die Preise sind für so eine gehobene Klasse absolut fair.

Einzig, in letzter Zeit habe ich kaum noch Plätze bekommen ohne mehrere Tage im Voraus reserviert zu haben. Das muss man definitiv rechtzeitig tun. Das spricht aber natürlich für und nicht gegen das Restaurant.

text:
Edit: This was our second visit, and we were once again absolutely thrilled. Just like on our first visit, we received an exceptionally warm welcome. Your staff is truly lovely and incredibly attentive without being intrusive – it makes you feel completely at ease. The food arrived very quickly, was beautifully presented, and of perfect quality. This time, we also tried the Umami Garlic Wagyu. It's a must-try; your marinade is truly unique. (I think I'll order it twice next time). And your Agedashi Tofu – I have no idea how you do it, but I've never had better. We left the restaurant full and satisfied, received a very friendly send-off, and thank you for a wonderful evening.

1st Review:

We combined a visit to Berlin with dinner at Ushido because we really wanted to try Wagyu. The restaurant has a pleasingly aesthetic design. The staff was exceptionally friendly, courteous, and, above all, attentive without being intrusive. The use of the teppanyaki grill was well explained, and we even received tips and suggestions on preparing and combining the ingredients. And our advice was spot on – using a sauce would have completely undermined and overshadowed the premium Wagyu beef. The Wagyu was truly an absolute highlight – we've never experienced anything like it before. It simply melts in your mouth. And the homemade lemonades... delicious!

Thank you for this unique culinary experience! We'll be back.

​Wir haben uns heute zu zweit komplett durch die Dim-Sum-Karte probiert. Kurz gesagt: In Deutschland habe ich noch keine besseren gegessen. Die Qualität des Essens ist überragend, der Service hochprofessionell und aufmerksam.
​Für Dim-Sum-Liebhaber in Berlin eine absolute Pflichtadresse. Wir kommen definitiv wieder.

placeAddress: Goji, Motzstraße 58, 10777 Berlin-Bezirk Tempelhof-Schöneberg, Germany
placeDescription: Classic southern Chinese dishes & dim sum dumplings & steamed buns in a venue with sidewalk tables.
text:
The three golden rules of Asian food are:

It must be served hot.

It must be spicy.

It must have just been alive
… to guarantee quality, freshness, and flavor.

All of this was wonderfully fulfilled.

We were lucky and didn't need a reservation, even though the place fills up relatively quickly and was quite busy. We even saw the waiter bring out an extra table for two for a couple to accommodate their request.

We ordered dumplings and dim sum. We had many options and relied on the waiter's advice, as he responded to our general suggestions with counter-proposals that absolutely convinced us. The sauces deserve special mention. They were very tasty and well-balanced in terms of spiciness (they also come in different strengths, but at Goji, spiciness is more about flavor than being excessive).

The focus should really be on the crunchy duck. It's low in fat, incredibly flavorful, and crunchy. This isn't just a thick layer of fried food, but rather thin, crunchy layers that melt in your mouth.

Afterwards, I was truly full and satisfied!

The excellent service also deserves special mention.

Thank you!
originalText:
Die 3 goldenen Regeln bei asiatischem Essen sind:
Es muss heiß serviert werden
Es muss scharf sein
Es muss gerade noch gelebt haben
… um die Qualität, Frische und Geschmack zu garantieren.
All dies wurde wunderbar erfüllt.
Wir hatten Glück und mussten nicht reservieren obwohl dieser Ort sich relativ schnell füllt und gut besucht war. Wir haben sogar gesehen, dass der Kellner einem Paar extra noch einen 2er Tisch rausgebracht hatte, um den Wünschen zu entsprechen.
Bestellt wurden Dumplings und Dim Sum. Hier hatten wir viele Optionen, haben uns auf den Rat des Kellners verlassen, da dieser auf unsere groben Richtungen die wir ihm gegeben haben mit Gegen-Vorschlägen kam, die uns absolut überzeugt haben. Hervorzuheben sind die Soßen dazu. Sehr leckere und gut angestimmte Schärfe (die gibt es auch in verschiedenen Stärken, Schärfe gilt bei Goji aber eher als Geschmack, als dass man maßlos übertreiben kann).
Der Fokus sollte nämlich auf der crunchy Ente liegen. Diese ist fettarm und super geschmackvoll und CRUNCHY. Das ist nicht einfach eine fette Frittierschicht, sondern eher dünne crunchy Schichten, die auf der Zunge zergehen.
Danach war ich echt satt und zufrieden!
Hervorzuheben ist auch der exzellente Service.

Danke!

placeAddress: Rutz, Chausseestraße 8, 10115 Berlin, Germany
placeDescription: Chic dining venue with creative, international dishes prepared by renowned chef Marco Müller.
text:
Dining at Rutz was, without question, an experience that demonstrates remarkable technical skill, creativity and precision. The restaurant has created an elegant and refined atmosphere, with a sophisticated dining room that immediately conveys why it has earned its Michelin recognition. The service team is attentive, professional and passionate.

However, there were aspects of the experience that prevented it reaching the exceptional standard I anticipated.

Throughout the evening there was a large number of staff involved in serving each course. While each server was courteous and knowledgeable, the constant rotation of servers made the experience feel fragmented. Different people would arrive to present, serve, clear or explain dishes, which at times became confusing rather than seamless. Fine dining should feel effortless and cohesive, but on this occasion the service felt over choreographed.

The cuisine is unquestionably imaginative and technically accomplished. Every plate resembled a carefully curated work of art, with meticulous presentation and evident attention to detail. However, there were several courses where the pursuit of artistic expression outweighed the enjoyment of the food itself. While visually captivating, dishes lacked depth of flavour and came across as restrained. Delicacy is one thing, but there were moments where subtlety crossed into blandness, leaving me wishing for more balance between visual creativity and taste.

I found the storytelling surrounding the dishes somewhat underdeveloped. Modern Michelin dining often succeeds because each course tells a story, whether about regional heritage, the chef’s philosophy, local producers or the inspiration behind the composition. At Rutz, many of the presentations felt limited to a straightforward description of the ingredients, essentially explaining what was on the plate rather than why it mattered. I had hoped to gain a greater appreciation of the history, cultural significance or creative journey behind each course. A richer narrative would have transformed the meal from an impressive technical display into a more emotionally engaging experience.

The wine pairing was another element that left mixed impressions. It began exceptionally well, with the opening selections complementing the early courses beautifully. The progression felt thoughtful, balanced and enhanced both the food and the wines themselves. Midway through the menu, however, the pairing lost direction. Some wines felt disconnected from the dishes, making the overall progression less coherent. Fortunately, the final stages of the pairing regained their focus, concluding with some excellent selections that restored confidence in the overall concept and provided a memorable finish to the evening.

Overall, Rutz undoubtedly deserves recognition for its innovation, technical execution and ambition. It offers an experience that many diners will admire, particularly those who appreciate culinary experimentation and artistic presentation.

For me, however, the evening highlighted that exceptional fine dining is about more than technical perfection. The most memorable restaurants create harmony between flavour, storytelling, service and atmosphere. While Rutz excels in creativity and craftsmanship, I left feeling that greater emphasis on flavour, more cohesive service and richer narratives behind each course would elevate the experience from impressive to truly unforgettable.

I would also encourage the restaurant to provide greater clarity during the reservation process regarding the €600 payment. It was not immediately apparent that this amount functions as a booking fee rather than being credited towards the final account. Clearer communication at the outset would help manage guests’ expectations.

With a total expenditure of €1,544 for the evening, I anticipated an experience that was exceptional in every respect. Unfortunately, I left still feeling hungry and, despite recognising the considerable technical skill and creativity involved, ultimately underwhelmed and disappointed.

text:
My wife and I dined at the Rutz wine bar last night and opted for the inspirational menu with eight wine pairings.

The evening began with an amuse-bouche that immediately set a high standard: finely sliced ​​potato cubes drizzled with a marjoram emulsion, accompanied by a drinking bowl filled with beef stock. This small dish, with its complexity, precision, and rich flavor, was the first highlight of the evening.

However, we found the flow of the following 60 minutes less than ideal. The first courses were served in what we felt was a very rapid succession. At times, the next wine was poured even before the previous one was nearly finished. This created a feeling of hecticness that significantly detracted from our enjoyment. Only after I explicitly requested that the pace be slowed did the rhythm ease.

The food itself was, for the most part, of a very high standard. The dishes were imaginative, unusual, and complexly composed without seeming arbitrary. With one exception, the wine pairings harmonized beautifully with each course. The young waitress who served us and the sommelier deserve special mention. Both were exceptionally friendly and attentive, and explained each course and wine with great expertise.

We were somewhat disappointed by the "Handschrift" course, consisting of aged and dried beef with wild mushrooms and lichen, accompanied by sliced ​​hazelnuts and a beef broth. The beef itself was first-rate and sliced ​​paper-thin, but its appearance strongly reminded me of carpaccio. The granules of wild mushrooms, lichen, and grated beef were rather subdued in flavor; the hazelnuts were the dominant flavor. It's important to emphasize that we certainly enjoyed the dish, but compared to the preceding courses, it lacked the same complexity and depth of flavor.


We were somewhat disappointed by the "Handschrift" course, consisting of aged and dried beef with wild mushrooms and lichen, accompanied by sliced ​​hazelnuts and a beef broth. The following dishes were once again very impressive. The seared carrot with chicken skin and tarragon was particularly striking. The chicken skin was located inside the carrot, creating a surprising yet perfectly harmonious flavor. The lamb dish with wild garlic was also well-balanced. The lamb itself was beautifully pink, though a little too firm for my personal taste.

To conclude, we were served three desserts. The strawberry with lemon balm and the pear with oxalic acid and koji mushroom were superbly prepared and once again demonstrated the kitchen's precision and creativity. The final dessert, however, was noticeably disappointing: a wild rose granita infused with pine needle and sandalwood essences. Unfortunately, these gave the dessert a slightly unpleasant, bath-like quality.

In summary, it was a wonderful evening with cuisine of impressive quality. The dishes were almost consistently excellent, creatively composed, and harmoniously presented. A few courses, particularly the aged beef and the wild rose granita, fell somewhat short of the high standard set by the rest of the menu, in our opinion. However, our most significant criticism wasn't directed at the kitchen, but rather at the initially rushed service. Once the pace was adjusted, we were able to enjoy a much more relaxed evening.

Overall, the service team was very friendly, attentive, and professionally competent. The explanations of the dishes and wines, in particular, enhanced the evening. Despite these minor shortcomings, the Rutz wine bar remains, for us, a place of great culinary ambition where we have experienced many memorable moments.
originalText:
Meine Frau und ich waren gestern Abend in der Weinbar Rutz essen und haben uns für das Inspirationsmenü mit acht Gläsern Weinbegleitung entschieden.

Der Abend begann kulinarisch mit einem Amuse-Gueule, das sofort Maßstäbe setzte. Ein fein in Scheiben geschnittener Kartoffelwürfel, beträufelt mit einer Majoran-Emulsion, dazu eine Trinkschale mit einem Auszug aus Rinderfond. Dieses kleine Gericht war in seiner Komplexität, Präzision und Geschmacksfülle das erste Highlight des Abends.

Weniger gelungen empfanden wir allerdings den Ablauf der folgenden etwa 60 Minuten. Die ersten Gänge wurden für unser Empfinden in sehr rascher Folge serviert. Teilweise wurde bereits der nächste Wein eingeschenkt, obwohl der vorherige noch nicht annähernd ausgetrunken war. Dadurch entstand bei uns ein Gefühl von Hektik, das den Genuss deutlich beeinträchtigte. Erst nachdem ich ausdrücklich darum gebeten hatte, das Tempo zu reduzieren, entspannte sich der Rhythmus.

Kulinarisch zeigte sich der Abend überwiegend auf sehr hohem Niveau. Die Gerichte waren phantasievoll, ausgefallen und komplex komponiert, ohne dabei beliebig zu wirken. Auch die Weinbegleitung harmonierte bis auf eine Ausnahme sehr schön mit den einzelnen Gängen. Besonders positiv hervorzuheben ist die junge Mitarbeiterin, die uns die Speisen servierte, sowie die Sommelière. Beide waren ausgesprochen freundlich, engagiert und erklärten die einzelnen Gänge und Weine mit großer Sachkenntnis.

Etwas enttäuscht waren wir vom Gang Handschrift, bestehend aus gereiftem und getrocknetem Rind mit Waldpilz und Flechte, dazu in Scheiben geschnittene Haselnüsse sowie eine Rinderbrühe. Das Rind selbst war erstklassig und hauchdünn geschnitten, erinnerte mich in der Anmutung jedoch stark an Carpaccio. Das Granulat aus Waldpilzen, Flechten und geraspeltem Rind blieb geschmacklich eher zurückhaltend; im Wesentlichen dominierten die Haselnüsse.  Wichtig ist zu betonen, das Gericht hat uns durchaus geschmeckt, aber im Vergleich zu den vorangegangenen Gängen fehlten ihm die gleiche Vielschichtigkeit und Geschmackstiefe.

Die folgenden Gerichte überzeugten uns dann wieder sehr. Besonders eindrucksvoll war die Sandkarotte mit Broilerhaut und Estragon. Die Broilerhaut befand sich im Inneren der Karotte und sorgte für eine überraschende, zugleich sehr stimmige Aromatik. Auch das Lammgericht mit Waldlauch war gut ausbalanciert. Das Lamm selbst war schön rosa gebraten, für meinen persönlichen Geschmack allerdings ein wenig zu fest.

Zum Abschluss folgten drei Desserts. Die Erdbeere mit Melisse sowie die Birne mit Oxalsäure und Kojipilz waren hervorragend zubereitet und zeigten erneut die Präzision und Kreativität der Küche. Das letzte Dessert fiel für uns dagegen spürbar ab, ein Granité mit Wildrosen, dem eine Fichtennadel-Essenz sowie Sandelholzessenz beigegeben war. Diese verlieh dem Dessert leider eine Note von Badezusatz.

Zusammenfassend war es ein sehr schöner Abend mit einer Küche von beeindruckender Qualität. Die Speisen waren fast durchgehend hervorragend gearbeitet, kreativ und stimmig komponiert. Einzelne Gänge, insbesondere das gereifte Rind und das Wildrosen-Granité, blieben aus unserer Sicht etwas hinter dem hohen Niveau der übrigen Menüfolge zurück. Der deutlichste Kritikpunkt betrifft jedoch nicht die Küche, sondern den anfänglich zu hektischen Serviceablauf. Nachdem das Tempo angepasst wurde, konnten wir den Abend wesentlich entspannter genießen.

Das Serviceteam war insgesamt sehr freundlich, aufmerksam und fachlich überzeugend. Besonders die Erläuterungen zu den Speisen und Weinen haben den Abend bereichert. Trotz kleiner Schwächen bleibt die Weinbar Rutz für uns ein Ort großer kulinarischer Ambition, an dem wir viele beeindruckende Momente erlebt haben.

I took my wife with me since I like strong flavours and she doesn't. Salt, spice, sweet, etc. I had someone that I could talk about the dishes and make sure I was being sensible.

All heavy savory dishes were oversalted. I thought I was crazy because oversalt my dishes at home and love it. Never to this extent though. I don't know if they wanted me to order more drinks or what but sad that the food was sacrificed for that reason.

All the other dishes were ok. They were good in the sense that I could've eaten them at a mid range restaurant and been happy. But being at a 3 star michelin place and this is the best they had to offer?

Just because something took longer to make or was more complex to create doesn't make the food better.

The one dish were I tasted something different and new for the first time was the dessert were natural Oxalsäure from vegetables is used. That was wonderful but one dish can't make up for the other 12.

I'm middle class and this experience was a huge part of my savings. I could keep on writing but I don't want to waste any more energy on this. Final bill was around 890 euro with tip.

text:
Dining at Rutz was one of the most memorable culinary experiences I’ve had in Berlin. From the moment I arrived, the atmosphere felt special but still relaxed and welcoming. The restaurant has a modern, elegant design, and the staff made me feel comfortable right away.
The tasting menu was truly impressive. Each dish arrived beautifully presented, almost like a small piece of art. What stood out most was the creativity of the flavors. Many of the ingredients were local and seasonal, yet the chef transformed them into something completely unique. Every course felt carefully thought out, with surprising combinations that worked perfectly together.
The service was outstanding throughout the evening. The staff explained each dish in detail and were very knowledgeable about the wine pairings. Their passion for the food and wine really added to the experience and made the meal feel more personal.
What I loved most about Rutz is that despite its three Michelin stars, it doesn’t feel intimidating. Instead, it feels like a place where you can truly enjoy food, discover new flavors, and spend a special evening. It’s definitely a restaurant I would recommend to anyone who wants to experience one of the best fine-dining restaurants in Berlin.

text:
We had made a reservation for our wedding anniversary based on numerous recommendations and requested a quiet table upstairs in a corner.

We were given a table downstairs, quite close between two others, in a very dark setting, which my husband absolutely hated.

The reason given was that the upstairs area was closed, even though it was busy and definitely not empty.

The server was so tense and nervous that we asked her if everything was alright. Yes, she said, she was just concentrating.

The food was good, but it lacked a cohesive theme.

What bothered us most was a political statement made on the way from the restroom to the restaurant. If there's one thing we don't want on an evening meant for enjoyment and relaxation, and which, admittedly, costs a fair amount, it's any kind of political commentary.

The staff can certainly make such statements in private, but not in public.

We were so annoyed that Rutz had ruined our day that my husband didn't want to go to a Michelin-starred restaurant again for a while.

I then invited him to Tim Raue's restaurant for my birthday. They did everything right and made my husband happy.

Perfect menu, excellent, professional, and relaxed staff, light and space 🙏 We shared our experience at Rutz there, and it has since been confirmed by acquaintances.
originalText:
Wir hatten für unseren Hochzeitstag auf vielfache Empfehlung reserviert und um einen ruhigen Tisch im Obergeschoss in einer Ecke gebeten.
Bekommen haben wir einen Tisch unten relativ dicht zwischen 2 anderen in sehr dunklem Ambiente, was meinem Mann überhaupt nicht gefällt.
Grund: oben wäre geschlossen, obwohl es oben unruhig war und definitiv nicht leer.
Die Servicekraft war so angespannt und nervös, dass wir sie fragten, ob alles in Ordnung ist. Ja, meinte sie, sie sei nur konzentriert.
Das Essen war gut, aber es fehlte uns ein roter Faden.
Was uns am meisten gestört hat, war ein politisches Statement auf dem Weg von der Toilette ins Restaurant. Wenn wir etwas nicht wollen an einem Abend, der Genuss und Entspannung vorbehalten ist und ja auch einiges kostet, so sind das jegliche politischen Äußerungen.
Das kann das Personal gerne in eigenen Räumlichen tun, aber nicht öffentlich.
Wir haben uns so geärgert, dass das Rutz uns diesen Tag verdorben hat, dass mein Mann erst mal kein Sternerestaurant mehr besuchen wollte.
Ich habe ihn dann zu meinem Geburtstag zu Tim Raue eingeladen. Sie haben alles richtig gemacht und meinen Mann versöhnlich gestimmt.
Perfektes Menü, exzellentes, souveränes und entspanntes Personal, Licht und Platz 🙏
Unsere Erfahrungen vom Rutz haben wir dort  berichtet und sie wurden inzwischen auch von Bekannten bestätigt.

text:
The food was delicious, and the vegetarian menu was also excellent! However, there were a few things that could be criticized in a 3-star restaurant.

The service seemed somewhat disorganized at times, and we overheard conversations and even discussions that weren't meant for our ears.

The constant movement around, with or without dishes, created a very restless atmosphere. The upbeat, sometimes too loud music towards the end of the evening, as well as the tidying up on the upper floor, was also irritating.

At the beginning, our meals were mixed up, so the lactose-containing course was served to the person with the intolerance. We also informed them at the start of the meal that we wouldn't be drinking alcohol, but at the end, we were presented with and offered a shot of schnapps. They apologized for this, but such a thing shouldn't happen.

Finally, other issues, such as not folding the napkins when we stood up, infrequent table cleaning, and the lack of petit fours, contributed to a mediocre experience.


Compared to other 3-star restaurants, this one unfortunately fell short of expectations.
originalText:
Das Essen war lecker und auch das Veggie-Menü war überzeugend! Jedoch gab es einige Punkte, die bei einem 3* Restaurant zu kritisieren sind.

Der Service wirkte teils unkoordiniert und wir bekamen Gespräche oder auch Diskussionen mit, die nicht für unsere Ohren bestimmt waren.
Die Atmosphäre wirkte durch das ständige rumgehen, mit oder ohne Geschirr, sehr unruhig. Ebenso die flottere, teils zu laute Musik gegen Ende des Abends sowie das Geräume (Aufräumen?) auf der oberen Etage war irritierend.

Zu Beginn wurde unser Essen vertauscht, so dass der laktosehaltige Gang der Person mit Intoleranz serviert wurde. placeDescription: Chic dining venue with creative, international dishes prepared by renowned chef Marco Müller.
text:
I hesitated for a long time about whether to write this review. However, after my last visit to Rutz, I feel compelled to share my experience – hoping that my concerns will be taken seriously this time.

I've been a regular customer for many years and have visited Rutz four to five times a year. The cuisine was, as usual, of the highest standard. Unfortunately, due to the service, and especially the wine service, I wasn't able to enjoy the meal as much as I normally would.

I had specifically requested a predominantly classic wine pairing beforehand, as I'm not a big fan of natural wines. The new sommelier, Mr. Sebastian Höpfner, assured me that this would be no problem. I was therefore all the more irritated when the wine pairing began with a natural wine – followed by two more. After the third glass, I stopped the wine pairing.

Even more disappointing was the complete lack of understanding or cooperation. The sommelier's reaction seemed more offended than solution-oriented – absolutely inappropriate for a three-Michelin-starred restaurant. If the requested wine pairing isn't feasible, I expect a clear recommendation for a bottle. That would have been the better solution.

The rest of the service also fell short of the usual standard: glasses weren't lifted while being poured, and the table was repeatedly spilled and not wiped clean. For a restaurant of this caliber, that's simply unacceptable.

The wine service, overall, felt more like a wine bar than a three-star establishment. I've never experienced anything like this at Rutz before – until this visit, the service had always been excellent, characterized by attentiveness and finesse.

Had this been a one-off, I probably would have given Rutz a second chance with Mr. Höpfner. However, since I've heard similar stories from friends and acquaintances about similar experiences with the new sommelier, I'll be staying away for the time being. For this price range, I expect reliability, professionalism, and above all, that agreements made with the guest are respected.

Perhaps this review will give you something to think about. Should the service return to its former quality, I will gladly return.

Sincerely,

L. H.
originalText:
Ich habe lange überlegt, ob ich diese Bewertung schreiben soll. Nach meinem letzten Besuch im Rutz sehe ich jedoch die Notwendigkeit, meine Erfahrung zu teilen – in der Hoffnung, dass mein Anliegen diesmal ernst genommen wird.

Ich bin seit vielen Jahren Stammgast und war vier- bis fünfmal im Jahr im Rutz. Die Küche war auch diesmal – wie gewohnt – auf höchstem Niveau. Leider konnte ich das Menü aufgrund des Services und vor allem aufgrund des Weinservices nicht so genießen wie sonst.

Ich hatte vorab ausdrücklich eine überwiegend klassische Weinbegleitung gewünscht, da ich kein großer Naturwein-Fan bin. Der neue Sommelier, Herr Sebastian Höpfner, bestätigte mir, dass dies problemlos möglich sei. Umso irritierter war ich, als die Weinbegleitung direkt mit einem Naturwein startete – gefolgt von zwei weiteren Naturweinen. Nach dem dritten Glas habe ich die Weinbegleitung abgebrochen.

Noch enttäuschender war, dass keinerlei Verständnis oder Einsicht gezeigt wurde. Die Reaktion des Sommeliers wirkte eher beleidigt als lösungsorientiert – für ein Drei-Sterne-Restaurant absolut unangebracht. Wenn die gewünschte Weinbegleitung nicht umsetzbar ist, erwarte ich eine klare Empfehlung für eine Flasche. Genau das wäre die bessere Lösung gewesen.

Auch der restliche Service entsprach nicht dem gewohnten Niveau: Die Gläser wurden beim Einschenken nicht angehoben, der Tisch wurde mehrfach vollgetropft und nicht abgewischt. Für ein Restaurant dieser Klasse ist das schlicht nicht akzeptabel.

Der Weinservice wirkte insgesamt eher auf dem Niveau einer Weinbar und nicht wie in einem Drei-Sterne-Haus. So etwas habe ich im Rutz bisher nie erlebt – bis zu diesem Besuch war der Service immer exzellent und geprägt von Aufmerksamkeit und Fingerspitzengefühl.

Wäre dies ein einmaliger Ausrutscher, hätte ich dem Rutz mit Herrn Höpfner vermutlich eine zweite Chance gegeben. Da mir jedoch inzwischen aus meinem Umfeld ähnliche Erfahrungen mit dem neuen Sommelier berichtet wurden, werde ich vorerst fernbleiben. Für diese Preisklasse erwarte ich Zuverlässigkeit, Professionalität und vor allem, dass Absprachen mit dem Gast respektiert werden.

Vielleicht regt diese Bewertung zum Nachdenken an. Sollte sich der Service wieder an frühere Qualitäten annähern, komme ich sehr gerne wieder.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
L. H.

text:
A Deeply Disappointing Experience at Rutz, Berlin

I booked a table at Rutz a month in advance and was genuinely excited. It was my first time visiting a 3-Michelin-star restaurant. I ordered the Berlin Style menu for €240 and expected a memorable, high-level experience. Unfortunately, the evening turned into a series of disappointments.

The problems began with the very first course. I’m vegetarian, while my partner eats meat, and the staff mixed up our dishes. I ended up eating an oxtail croquette by mistake, my first bite of meat in five years. The only response I received was a brief “sorry,” with no real apology, no compensation, and no attempt to acknowledge the seriousness of the mistake.

Additionally, even though we clearly said we didn’t want any wine, the staff pushed us to “just try one glass.” Only when the bill arrived did we discover that each glass cost €40.

The menu price was also incorrect. We were charged €260 instead of the €240 shown at the time of booking. When I asked why, I was told that the price had gone up since then, even though I reserved a month earlier. This felt extremely unprofessional and unfair.

The meal lasted 3.5 hours, with long and uncomfortable gaps between courses. At one point we waited nearly 30 minutes for the next dish.

Overall, a very disappointing experience that fell far short of what one would expect from a 3-Michelin-star restaurant.

The experience exceeded all of our expectations. The flavors are rich and profound, the textures and combinations are incredible - pairings I would never imagine could work, yet they did - and in a way that surpassed anything we anticipated.
After each course, the cutlery is replaced with pieces tailored specifically to the next dish. The sensory experience (from the presentation of the dishes, to their aroma, to the act of eating them) is unlike anything we’ve encountered.
We chose the 13-course menu and enjoyed nearly four hours of exceptional experience. You truly feel like you’re on a genuine culinary journey, and as though you leave differently than you came in.
Our experience was guided by Lili, an intelligent, polite, and remarkably attentive server. We were blown away by her professionalism, kindness, and a level of service that is nothing less than the best we’ve ever received. It genuinely felt like she enjoys what she does, and that feeling reached us at the table. We have nothing but gratitude for her and the entire team.

placeAddress: Rutz, Chausseestraße 8, 10115 Berlin, Germany
placeDescription: Chic dining venue with creative, international dishes prepared by renowned chef Marco Müller.
text:
Let's start with the food: there are three aperitifs, the first served in the shape of a lollipop – a fun touch, and the foliage around it serves as table decoration after the amuse-bouche. This is followed by mussel and sorrel with a wonderful texture, and a savory praline. Overall, a varied and delicious start (9/10).

Restaurant manager Falco Mühlichen explains the intention behind the restaurant's focus on sustainability and showing what can be achieved with "ordinary ingredients," rather than flaunting luxury products.

In addition to a red wine, I choose several non-alcoholic drinks from the selection, which the chef curates around each dish. The flavor profile of the drinks isn't always to my taste.

The first substantial flavor explosion comes with the first course, called Salad & Poppy Seed – this actually consists of grilled and fermented romaine lettuce, a poppy seed semifreddo, and homemade, ash-ripened fresh cheese (absolutely fantastic, 10/10).

The homemade sourdough bread is traditionally served with a black pudding praline – a bit too heavy in the context of the overall menu – but delicious nonetheless. The bread is served on hot stones – clever.

With the second course, the kitchen spectacularly demonstrates that trout can be transformed into a wonderful dish. Fabulous texture, a wonderful contrast with the buttermilk broth, and a touch of crunch to play with your mouth (another 10)

Not quite as exciting was the yellowtail mackerel – expertly served in a spicy tomato essence with oil (9)

Highly intriguing in its preparation, although not quite to my taste (somewhat one-dimensional compared to the previous courses) – a beetroot praline – pan-fried in Wagyu fat with horseradish and a delicate burnt cream sauce (8.5) – a welcome respite for the palate.

An interlude outside the menu, from my favorite category of "this shouldn't possibly go together" – crème fraîche, white chocolate, celery ice cream, and hazelnut crumble – surprisingly harmonious and flavorful – a welcome addition (9.5)

The menu then continued with the male sturgeon, served on two potato slices with Arctic char caviar. An elegant final fish course. (8)

Pure visual understatement in the first meat course. Presented in its finished form, the discerning diner has no idea what to expect. Well: an extraordinary combination of Wagyu strips, kohlrabi sauerkraut, and a divine kohlrabi broth. Finished with a hollandaise made from bone marrow. (9.5)

The "Chicken and Leek" course consists of two parts. An incredibly intense opener with liver and rhubarb, which unfortunately promises more than the second part can deliver. The meat has a really good texture, but the flavor is rather bland. The attractive side dish of leek hearts and chanterelles doesn't redeem the overall impression for me. (7)

The pre-dessert, to which Chef Marco Müller says "Good day," is a masterful palate cleanser. Gooseberry, Berliner Weisse (9). Dessert arrives with variations of raspberry (fresh, dried, and rehydrated) and a delicate dill-raspberry kombucha. Hidden within is buffalo milk ice cream. The cucumber strips placed on top serve as a contrast to the sweetness of the raspberries, but in my opinion, they weren't necessary. (9)

Redcurrant granita with a zabaglione flavored with roasted yeast concludes the meal. Tasty, but somewhat underwhelming for a finale. (7)

The service team is relaxed and always up for a laugh. The enthusiasm with which they describe each dish, from its centerpiece to the last detail, is remarkable—at Rutz, they take pride in what they serve, and rightly so.

I have rarely experienced a restaurant where the individual ingredients are prepared with such meticulous care. The sheer amount of pickling, fermenting, curing, preserving, dehydrating, and salting is unparalleled—all, of course, for the sake of pure enjoyment. The first half of the menu, which with few exceptions was sourced regionally, was significantly more exciting than the second part.
originalText:
Starten wir direkt mit dem Essen: es gibt drei Aperos, der erste serviert in Lollyform, witzig und das Gestrüpp außenrum dient nach dem Gruß als Tischschmuck. Danach Muschel & Sauerampfer mit toller Textur der Muschel und eine Bohnenkraut Praline. Insgesamt ein abwechslungsreicher Start (9/10)

Restaurantleiter Falco Mühlichen erklärt die Intention mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit und weniger mit Luxusprodukten protzen als vielmehr zeigen, was man mit "normalen Zutaten" als Geschmack herausholen kann

Ich wähle neben einem Rotwein einige Getränke aus der alkoholfreien Begleitung, diese wird vom Chef um das Gericht herum kreiert. Das Geschmacksprofil der Drinks ist nicht immer meins

Die erste substantielle Geschmacksexplosion kommt mit dem ersten Gang, der Salat & Mohn genannt wird - dahinter verbirgt sich gegrillter und fermentierter Romana, ein Mohn Semifreddo und selbst hergestellter, in Asche gereifter Frischkäse (sehr geil, 10/10)

Zum selbst hergestellten Sauerteigbrot gibt es traditionell eine Blutwurstpraline - ein bisschen zu schwer im Kontext des Gesamtmenüs - aber lecker. Das Brot wird auf heißen Steinen serviert - clever

Beim zweiten Gang beweist die Küche auf spektakuläre Weise, dass man aus Forelle ein wunderbares Gericht zaubern kann. Sagenhafte Textur, ein toller Kontrast mit dem Buttermilchsud und dazu zum Spielen im Mund ein bisschen Knusper (erneut 10)

Nicht ganz so aufregend die Gelbschwanzmakrele - in einer würzigen Tomatenessenz mit Öl souverän serviert (9)

Von der Zubereitung her hochspannend , wenngleich geschmacklich nicht ganz für mich (etwas eindimensional im Vergleich zu den vorherigen Gängen) - eine Rote Beete Praline - ausgebraten in Wagyufett und mit Meerrettich und einem feinen gebrannten Sahnesösschen (8,5) - der Gaumen bekommt etwas Erholung

Ein Einschub außerhalb des Menüs aus meiner Lieblingskategorie „das kann eigentlich gar nicht zusammenpassen“ - Creme fraiche, weiße Schokolade, Sellerieeis und Haselnusscrumble - erstaunlich stimmig  und geschmacklich - eine gute Erweiterung (9,5)

Im Menü folgt dann der männliche Stör, der auf zwei Kartoffelscheiben und mit Saiblingkaviar serviert wird. Ein eleganter letzter Fischgang. (8)

Optisches understatement pur im ersten Fleischgang. Fertig angerichtet hat der geneigte Esser keine Ahnung, was ihn erwartet. Nun: eine außerordentliche Kombination aus Wagyustreifen, Kohlrabi-Sauerkraut und einem göttlichen Kohlrabisud. Abgerundet  mit einer aus Knochenmark hergestellten Hollandaise. (9,5)

Der Gang „Huhn und Lauch“ besteht  aus zwei Teilen. Einem unglaublich intensiven Opener mit Leber und Rhabarber, der leider mehr verspricht, als der zweite Teil halten kann. Das Fleisch ist von der Textur wirklich gut, geschmacklich aber wenig sagend. Die schöne Beilage aus Lauchherzen und Pfifferlingen reißt den Gesamteindruck für mich nicht heraus (7)

Das Predessert, zu dem Chef Marco Müller "Guten Tag" sagt, ist ein souveräner Palate Cleanser. Stachelbeere, Berliner Weiße (9). Der Nachtisch kommt mit Variationen von Himbeere (frisch, getrocknet und rehydriert) und mit feiner Dill-Himbeer-Kombucha. Darin versteckt ist Büffelmilcheis. Die darauf platzierten Gurkenstreifen dienen als Kontrast zu der Süsse der Himbeeren, wären aus meiner Sicht aber nicht nötig gewesen. (9)

Johannisbeergranita mit einer Zabaione aromatisiert mit gerösteter Hefe beendet das Menü. Lecker aber etwas unspektakulär für einen Abschluss (7)

Das Serviceteam ist locker und immer für einen Spaß zu haben, ausfällig ist die Freude, mit der die Gerichte vom Mittelpunkt bis zum letzten Detail beschrieben werden - im Rutz ist man stolz darauf, was serviert wird - und das mit gutem Recht.

Selten habe ich ein Restaurant erlebt, bei dem die einzelnen Zutaten so aufwändig präpariert werden. Die Menge an „einlegen, fermentieren, beizen, konservieren, dehydrieren und salzen“ sucht ihresgleichen - natürlich im Sinne des Genusses. Die erste Hälfte des mit wenig Ausnahmen regional gesourcten Menüs war allerdings deutlich aufregender als der zweite Abschnitt.

text:
At the entrance of the restaurant, there was a large menu that we wanted to read. Even there, a man in a chef's hat and striking clothing approached us, more or less urging people to enter. He sat/stood at the entrance the entire time we ate, luring other people over and being very pushy. He was practically forcing them in.

The food arrived very quickly. For a starter, we had bruschetta (€6, 3 pieces), which was really delicious.

I ordered a tarte flambée Alsatian style (€14) and received a piece of pizza dough with some crème fraîche, cheese, and bacon bits and onion pieces carelessly slapped on top (see picture). My companion and I suspect it was even store-bought, ready-made dough. We're not entirely sure. It certainly had nothing to do with tarte flambée.

My companion ordered gnocchi filled with ricotta, with mozzarella and tomato sauce. For almost €18. The mozzarella was cold, the tomato sauce tasted awful, and there were maybe 10 soggy gnocchi in total. They were a bit large, but for that price, it's outrageous.

The service wasn't exactly friendly either. The coasters/beverage mats were just thrown on the table, and we had to remind them twice that we wanted to pay.

By the way, charging €3.90 for a 0.25l bottle of water and €7.50 for a 0.75l bottle is ridiculous.
originalText:
Am Eingang des Restaurants war eine große Speisekarte, die wir uns durchlesen wollten. Schon dort ist uns ein Mann mit Kochmütze und auffälliger Kleidung entgegengekommen, der die Leute mehr oder weniger dazu gedrängt hat, das Restaurant zu betreten. Er saß/stand die ganze Zeit am Eingang, während wir gegessen haben und hat weitere Personen zu sich gelockt und war sehr aufdringlich. Er hat sie wirklich regelrecht gezwungen.
Das Essen kam sehr schnell. Als Vorspeise gab’s Bruschetta (6€, 3 Stück), was echt lecker war.
Ich habe einen Flammkuchen Elsässer Art (14€) bestellt und habe ein Stück Pizzateig mit etwas Schmand, Käse und lieblos draufgeklatschten Speckwürfel und Zwiebelstücken bekommen (siehe Bild). Meine Begleitung und ich vermuten, dass es sogar gekaufter Fertigteig war. Sicher sind wir uns nicht. Mit Flammkuchen hatte das auf jeden Fall nichts zu tun.
Für meine Begleitung war es Gnochi gefüllt mit Ricotta, dazu Mozarella und Tomatensauce. Für fast 18€. Das Mozarella war kalt, die Tomatensauce schmeckte nicht und ingesamt waren es vielleicht 10 matschige Gnocchis. Sie waren zwar auch etwas größer, aber für den Preis ist das echt frech.
Die Bedienung war auch nicht gerade freundlich. Die Bierdeckel/Untersetzer wurden auf den Tisch geschmissen und wir mussten zwei mal darauf aufmerksam machen, dass wir gerne bezahlen möchten.

text:
It was a unique culinary journey with a diverse range of flavors. The service was very personal, almost friendly, without being intrusive.

We felt right at home from the moment we stepped into the restaurant.

Upon entering, you can see into the open kitchen. The overall design is very open, airy, warm, and timeless.

We ordered both the vegan and the fish eight-course menus, which, considering the quality of the food, the sophistication, the service, and the time we spent there (3.5 hours), were more than reasonably priced.

We would also like to commend the beverage pairings (one alcoholic and one non-alcoholic). The non-alcoholic pairings, in particular, were absolutely exceptional and unique, so we were eager to discover what flavor would come next with each course.

Each course is served on handcrafted ceramics made by the owner, emphasizing the connection to nature and the uniqueness of the food and the overall concept.

We will never forget this visit and hope to return soon.

Thank you again to the entire team.
originalText:
Es war eine einmalige kulinarische Reise mit verschiedensten Geschmäckern. Der Service war sehr persönlich, fast freundschalftlich, ohne dabei zu aufdringlich zu sein.
Wir haben uns beim ersten Schritt in das Lokal wie zu Hause gefühlt.
Gleich beim Eintreten kann man in die offene Küche schauen. Generell ist alles sehr offen, luftig, warm und zeitlos gestaltet.
Wir haben einmal das vegane und einmal das Fisch-8-Gänge Menü bestellt, das preislich angesichts der Qualität der Speisen, der Raffinesse, des Servicees und der dort verbrachten Zeit (3,5h), mehr als angebracht war.
Ebenso möchten wir die Getränkebegleitung (1x alkoholische und 1x alkoholfreie) positiv hervorheben. Gerade die alkoholfreien war absolut außergewöhnlich und einmalig sodass wir bei jedem Gang aufs neue gespannt gewesen sind, welcher Geschmack und wohl als nächstes erwartet.
Jeder Gang wird wird auf handgefertigter Keramik der Eigentümererin angerichtet und unterstreicht so die Naturverbundenheit und Einzigartigkeit der Speisen und des Konzepts.

Wir werden diesen Besuch wohl nie vergessen und hoffentlich bald wieder kommen.

Vielen Dank nochmals an das gesamte Team.
ownerResponseText:
Dear Johannes Herdtle,

Thank you so much for the glowing review. We look forward with great enthusiasm to every evening we can make unforgettable for our guests. You're absolutely right: our connection to nature brings everything together. :) Sincerely, Jinok Kim
ownerResponseOriginalText:
Lieber Johannes Herdtle,
vielen Dank für die überschwengliche Bewertung. Wir freuen uns voller Leidenschaft auf jeden Abend, den wir für die Gäste unvergesslich machen können. Sie haben recht: die Naturverbundenheit bringt alles zusammen. :)
Herzlich
Jinok Kim

text: The plating is exceptional in this restaurant. All of the food is served on hand built ceramics which is pretty beautiful. The flavors are really authentic to Korea. There were some novel use of fermentation which I quite enjoyed. There were some tastes that I had actually never experienced before as someone that has both visited Korea and also had Korean heritage. Having said that to be honest, I wasn’t blown away by the main courses. We had both vegan bebimbop  as well as the Neck of the pork today.  From the other reviews, it sounds like the food is rotated so perhaps this is a non-issue from other meals but when I go to a fine dining restaurant, I really would like for there to be something special in the main course. My main course was the vegan Plate and it was just some small Bachchan with some rice served with a radish top soup and some vegetable based sauce. I’ve had Korean food and a lot of different context and to be honest I’ve had a lot of bibimbop in my life and it’s one of my favorite dishes. This one just didn’t do anything for me. The tofu dish right before it was also just OK. The tofu is handmade, but you can get handmade tofu pretty abundantly in Seattle, where we’re from so again, it was hard to justify that this was an entire dish. Perhaps in Berlin this is more novel and I understand that due to a different audience this might be really interesting but for me, it was just OK.  If you’re not used to a lot of Korean food, it was a great experience. I’m sure because it was really for the most part. Well done. I love the fact that they have natural wines as a wine pairing. I did like all of the wines except for the last one and I really like the mission that this restaurant has so I really wanted to give it five stars, but I just couldn’t.

text:
There were two of us and we chose the veggie and fish menus.
I have to say, it was a real pleasure to get a glimpse into authentic Korean food culture.
About the ambiance: Seeing the various ceramics made by the chef herself upstairs – which, of course, are also used for the food – is simply fantastic. We went upstairs between courses and were able to look at them at our leisure.

About the service: I don't think we've ever been served so warmly. She was welcoming, had something to say and advise us on everything, and you could see that she really enjoyed doing it. Overall, NaNum has a very friendly and informal feel. Simply inviting.

About the food: (It should be noted that tastes differ)
The food was, above all, exciting. Wonderful new flavors that aren't common in Germany. The dry-aged fish, for example, simply delighted me.
There are, however, minor criticisms: There were some courses that simply lacked a bit in complexity or intensity. The seared asparagus with sesame salt and sesame sauce is good in itself, but the ingredients are generally very flat and one-dimensional. A little more spice would have been appropriate, or perhaps something more umami-like.

I also didn't need a rice cracker for the first course. The usual dish was delicious fish chips and seaweed chips with garlic stalks and fermented quince. The rice cracker practically sucked out all the flavor. Some dishes also lacked finesse in other areas, but these are, of course, minor issues and shouldn't be considered a complaint, as the cooking is of a high standard.


Overall, it was a very pleasant evening there.
originalText:
Wir waren zu zweit und haben das Veggie - sowie das Fischmenu ausgewählt.
Ich muss sagen, dass es eine echte Freude war, einen Einblick in wirklich koreanische Esskultur zu bekommen.
Zum Ambiente: Dass oben unterschiedliche von der Chefin selbst hergestellte Keramik zu sehen - die natürlich auch für das Essen benutzt werden - ist einfach nur toll. Wir sind zwischen den Gängen nach oben gegangen und konnten uns das in Ruhe angucken.

Zum Service: Ich glaube, so freundlich wurden wir noch nie bedient. Sie war herzlich, konnte uns zu allem was sagen und beraten und man konnte sehen, dass sie auch wirklich  Lust hatte das zu tun. Allgemein wirkt das im NaNum sehr freundlich und familiär. Einfach einladend.

Zum Essen: (Es sei angemerkt, dass Geschmäcker unterschiedlich sind)
Das Essen war vor allein eins: Spannend. Schöne neue Geschmäcker, die so in Deutschland nicht üblich sind. Dry age fish bspw. hat mich einfach begeistert.
Kleine Kritikpunkte gibt es jedoch: Es gab Gänge, die einfach wenig an Komplexität bzw. Intensität gefehlt hatten. Geflämmter Spargel mit Sesamsalz und Sesamsoße ist an sich gut, jedoch von den Komponenten allgemein sehr flach vom Geschmack und eindimensional. Da hätte eine Schärfe zum Verstärken oder auch etwas in Richtung Umami gepasst.
Auch beim Gruß aus der Küche hätte ich keinen Reiscracker gebraucht. Man hatte sonst schöne Fischchips bzw. Algenchips gehabt mit Knoblauchstängel und fermentiert er Quitte. Der Reiscracker saugt quasi jeden Geschmack weg. An anderen Ecken fehlte es bei manchen Gericht auch an Finesse, aber das sind natürlich nur Kleinigkeiten und sollte bitte nicht als Beschwerde angesehen werden, da es natürlich Kochen auf hohem Niveau ist.

Allgemein war es ein sehr schöner Abend dort.

text:
A Korean restaurant specializing in fermented dishes made with ingredients from their own garden or the surrounding area. On Wednesdays and Thursdays, you can choose between two set menus (vegetarian or with meat, which change every few weeks), each containing five different courses. Apparently, they offer fish menus on weekends, but we didn't have the chance to try them.

The food here is worth every penny. The two set menus are very well-balanced (as is the optional wine pairing), and the portions are just right – you'll leave feeling satisfied but not stuffed (and there's still room for one of their excellent desserts). Each course is briefly presented along with the wine, so you know exactly what you're eating.

The ambiance is also very pleasant, thanks in part to the friendly and attentive service. The very nice chef checked on us several times throughout the evening and answered our questions kindly. We felt very comfortable during the two hours we spent there and will definitely come back on our next visit to Berlin.

I can highly recommend this restaurant, even if you've never tried Korean cuisine before. None of the dishes were intimidating, even for those unfamiliar with it. You'll have a culinary experience that you'll remember for a long time.
originalText:
Ein koreanisches Restaurant welches sich auf fermentierte Speisen mit Zutaten aus dem eigenen Garten oder der Gegend spezialisiert hat. Mittwoch und Donnerstags kann man zwischen zwei Menus (vegetarisch oder mit Fleisch, wechseln alle paar Wochen) wählen welche 5 verschiedene Gänge beinhaltet. Am Wochenende gibt es anscheinend Menus mit Fisch, was wir aber nicht testen konnten.

Das Essen hier ist jeden Cent wert. Die beiden Menus die es zur Auswahl gibt sind sehr gut aufeinander (und die dazu zubuchbare Weinbegeleitung)abgestimmt und sind auch von den Portionen so, dass man gut gesättigt aber nicht überfüllt das Restauarant verlässt (für einen der hervoragenden Nachtische ist auch noch Platz). Jeder Gang wird zusammen mit dem Wein auch kurz vorgestellt, so dass man auch weiß was man hier ist.

Das Ambiente ist auch sehr angenehm, was auch an dem freundlichen und zuvorkommenden Servicepersonal liegt. Auch die sehr nette Köchin hat sich mehrmals im laufe des Abends nach dem Wohlbefinden erkundigt und auch nett auf Fragen geantwortet. Wir haben uns den die zwei Stunden die wir dort verbracht haben sehr wohl gefühlt und werden bei unserem nächsten Berlinbesuch auf jeden Fall wieder kommen.

Ich kann dieses Restaurant nur empfehlen, auch wenn man bis jetzt noch keinen Kontakt zur koreanischen Küche hatte. Von den Speißen war nichts dabei vor dem man Angst haben muss auch wenn man es nicht kennt. Man bekommt aber ein kulinarisches Erlebnis, an welches man sich noch lange erinnern wird

text:
I've been to India several times and am also a regular at Spice Village on Tempelhofer Damm. So, I'm certainly quite discerning when it comes to Indian cuisine.

The food here was okay, but nothing special. I'd still give the restaurant another chance.

What really bothered me, though, was how they handled leftovers. If you want to take leftovers home, you have to pack them yourself in your own containers. In other restaurants, the server takes the plates and packs the food for the guests. Even when I asked, this wasn't possible. The waitress explained that she was expressly forbidden from doing so and that guests had to do it themselves.

Especially with children, I find this policy not very customer- or family-friendly. Therefore, I unfortunately can't give it a better rating today.

text:
Since discovering this restaurant, we've been here at least six times – and deservedly so!

Food:

The food is simply incredibly delicious (you can see our favorites in the photo). Truly 5/5 stars; we'd even give it 10 if we could. Everything is perfectly seasoned, with unique and authentic flavors that you just don't find everywhere. Every dish tastes fresh, intense, and prepared with love. The chef's specials and burgers were also unbelievably delicious (unfortunately, no photo). For us, it's definitely the best Indian restaurant in Berlin right now, and we've tried quite a few!

Service:
The service is always friendly, attentive, and warm.

Atmosphere:
The atmosphere is also pleasant and cozy. These days, you should definitely make a reservation if you want a table – completely understandable given the quality! Everything is clean and well-maintained, including the restrooms.
originalText:
Seitdem wir dieses Restaurant entdeckt haben, waren wir inzwischen mindestens sechs Mal hier – und das absolut verdient!

Für uns aktuell definitiv das beste indische Restaurant in Berlin  und wir haben wirklich schon sehr viele ausprobiert!

Service:
Der Service ist jedes Mal freundlich, aufmerksam und herzlich.

Ambiente:
Auch das Ambiente ist angenehm und gemütlich. Mittlerweile sollte man auf jeden Fall reservieren, wenn man einen Platz bekommen möchte, absolut verständlich bei der Qualität! Alles ist sauber und gepflegt, auch die Toiletten.

text:
The food was good, but the price-performance ratio is somewhat unbalanced. I had the Königsberger Klopse (meatballs). The portion was more like a "senior citizen's portion at a Delicious price." The taste was okay, but you shouldn't expect the traditional, hearty style of this dish. Overall, the seasoning could be better, and the portion size should be more in line with the price. I saw several guests adding extra seasoning to their food. The dark beer was decent and reasonably priced. I'm deducting two stars for the service because there were several instances of confusion, requiring multiple inquiries and significant assistance from guests to help with order placement. This should be handled better in a restaurant of this price range. Overall, the experience felt a bit like a cafeteria, even though the otherwise pleasantly furnished dining room promised something different.

It's fine for a one-off visit. For regular patrons, the service, atmosphere, and value for money need improvement. The outdoor seating area, in addition to the modern interior, is definitely a plus.

Das Essen war gut - steht allerdings in einem etwas unausgewogenem Preis-Leistungsverhältnis. Ich hatte die Königsberger Klopse. Die Portion war eher eine 'Rentnerportion zum Deliciouspreis'. Geschmacklich war es ok, aber man sollte nicht die gutbürgerliche traditionelle Art dieses Gerichtes erwarten. Insgesamt könnte es besser mit Gewürzen abgestimmt sein und die Portionsgröße dem Preis entsprechen. Mehrere Gäste sah ich zum Nachwürzen ihrer Gerichte veranlasst. Das Dunkelbier war in Ordnung und auch preislich angemessen. Der Service bekommt bei mir zwei Sterne abgezogen, weil es doch mehrfach zu Verwirrung, mehrfachen Nachfragen und deutlicher Mithilfe bei der Zuordnung durch die Gäste kommen musste. Das sollte in einem Restaurant dieser Preisklasse besser funktionieren. Insgesamt bekam das Ganze so eher ein wenig Kantinencharakter, obwohl das sonstige Ambiente des angenehm eingerichteten Gastraumes eigentlich etwas Anderes versprach.

Für einen einmaligen Besuch in Ordnung. Für regelmäßige Besuche dürfte hier an Service, Atmosphäre und Preis-Leistung nachjustiert werden. Der Außenbereich ist, neben dem modernen Innenbereich eindeutig ein zusätzlicher Pluspunkt.

text:
A good start, somewhat disappointing at the end

The evening began promisingly, but faltered somewhat towards the end. The wait of around 60 minutes for the food was particularly long.

The food itself was generally good. The risotto was excellent – ​​beautifully creamy, pleasantly flavorful, and perfectly seasoned, neither too salty nor bland. The fish was tender, but unfortunately rather small for the price. The schnitzel was okay, nothing special, but fairly priced. The baked shrimp were tasty and also reasonably priced, although some of the shrimp in the second portion were unfortunately still raw.

The service was friendly and attentive, despite the long wait times.

A major plus is the location in the Nikolaiviertel, one of Berlin's oldest and most beautiful districts. The ambiance is reminiscent of a classic tavern or beer garden with fish and water features. The high ceilings and harmonious design create a particularly pleasant atmosphere.
originalText:
Gut gestartet, am Ende etwas enttäuschend

Der Abend begann vielversprechend, ließ jedoch zum Ende hin etwas nach. Besonders die Wartezeit von rund 60 Minuten auf das Essen war deutlich zu lang.

Geschmacklich war das Essen insgesamt solide. Das Risotto war sehr gelungen – schön cremig, angenehm mundig und perfekt abgeschmeckt, weder zu salzig noch fade. Der Fisch war zart, fiel für den Preis jedoch leider recht klein aus. Das Schnitzel war in Ordnung, allerdings kein besonderes Highlight, dafür preislich fair. Die gebackenen Garnelen waren lecker und ebenfalls angemessen bepreist, wobei bei der zweiten Portion einige Garnelen leider noch roh waren.

Der Service war freundlich und bemüht, trotz der längeren Wartezeiten.

Ein großer Pluspunkt ist die Lage im Nikolaiviertel, einem der ältesten und schönsten Viertel Berlins. Das Ambiente erinnert an ein klassisches Wirtshaus beziehungsweise einen Biergarten mit Fisch- und Wasserelementen. Besonders die hohen Decken und das stimmige Design schaffen eine angenehme Atmosphäre.

placeAddress: Fischer & Lustig, Poststraße 26, 10178 Berlin, Germany
text:
In January, I was looking for a restaurant to celebrate my 60th birthday with my guests. Since I didn't want anything too touristy, the Nikolaiviertel (St. Nicholas Quarter) didn't initially appeal to me. Nevertheless, we went from restaurant to restaurant, and I didn't want to go into "Fischer und Lustig" because I'd been to "Jäger und Lustig" and hadn't enjoyed it as much.

My husband persuaded me, and we opened the door. We were greeted very warmly and given a thorough tour of the restaurant. After a tasting, I knew this was the restaurant for me! The deciding factors were the service, the high-quality and delicious food, the warm plates, and the tasty drinks served in stylish glasses. I made the reservation that same day and contacted the sales office about four weeks before the event. I opted for the seasonal menu, and we could choose from three main courses. We were also able to change the soup and side dish for the main course for guests who didn't eat asparagus. I found that very accommodating, and the price was very reasonable.

Yesterday (May 2nd, 2026), the day finally arrived, and we came at 5:00 PM. Two tables were set for me and my guests in the restaurant garden (the weather was nice enough). We were greeted with a sparkling wine, which tasted very good, and my guests were even invited to sing for me! The tables were nicely set, and each guest received a menu. The asparagus soup arrived almost simultaneously for everyone, served in warm bowls with very fresh bread. The main courses, depending on the selection, were of high quality. I had the roast beef with asparagus, cooked to perfection, and the hollandaise/brown butter was served separately in small pitchers. Excellent! Again, almost all the plates arrived at once and were still hot. The dessert left nothing to be desired: the sour cream pudding wasn't too sweet, the strawberries were fresh, and the sorbet was delicious. All in all, a perfect meal!

The drinks were served in beautiful, labeled glasses, and they were also of very high quality. The white wine, a Pinot Gris, had a wonderful color and tasted light and fresh.

My two little guests were also well looked after, and they enjoyed their meal.

The service was friendly, attentive, and unobtrusive; everything was discussed with me beforehand.

I highly recommend the team at the "Fischer und Lustig" restaurant and would like to thank them again for this wonderful birthday dinner. We'll be back!
originalText:
Ich war im Januar auf der Suche nach einem Restaurant in dem ich zu meinem 60. Geburtstag mit meinen Gästen zu Abend essen kann. Da es nicht zu touristisch sein sollte, war mir das Nikolaiviertel erst gar nicht so recht. Wir gingen trotzdem von Restaurant zu Restaurant und ich wollte ins „Fischer und Lustig“ nicht rein, weil ich das „Jäger und Lustig“ kenne und es mir dort nicht so gefallen hat.
Mein Mann überzeugte mich und wir öffneten die Tür , wurden sehr freundlich begrüßt und uns das Restaurant mit einer „Hausdurchsuchung“ ausführlich nahe gebracht. Nach einem Probeessen war für mich klar, das wird mein Restaurant! Ausschlaggebend war der Service, qualitativ gutes und schmackhaftes Essen, warme Teller und auch leckere Getränke in stylischen Gläsern. Noch am selber Tag machte ich die Reservierung fest und setzte mich ca. 4 Wochen vor dem Termin mit dem Verkaufsbüro in Verbindung. Ich entschied mich für das Saisonmenü und wir konnten aus drei Hauptgerichten wählen. Auch durften wir bei den Gästen die keinen Spargel essen, bei der Vorsuppe und die Beilage beim Hauptgericht ändern. Das empfand ich sehr kulant und der Preis war für mich sehr angenehm.
Gestern nun( 2.5.2026) war es soweit und wir trafen um 17:00 Uhr ein. Zwei Tafeln waren für mich und meine Gäste im Restaurant Garten vorbereitet ( das Wetter ließ es ja zu). Es gab zum Empfang einen Rissecco der sehr gut schmeckte und meine Gäste durften für mich auch singen! Die Tische waren nett eingedeckt und für jeden Gast gab es eine Menükarte. Die Spargelsuppe kam für alle fast gleichzeitig und in warmen Teller mit sehr frischem Brot serviert. Das Hauptgericht je nach Auswahl qualitativ hochwertig, ich hatte das Roastbeef mit Spargel, auf den Punkt gegart und die Hollandaise/ braune Butter extra in kleinen Kännchen. Prima! Auch hier wieder fast alle Teller  gleichzeitig und warm. Das Dessert ließ auch keinen Wunsch offen, der Schmandpudding nicht süß, die Erdbeeren frisch und das Sorbet lecker. Alles in allem ein rundes Menü!
Die geeichten Getränke in schönen Gläsern mit Aufschrift und auch hier sehr wertig. Der Weißwein, ein Grauburgunder, hatte eine tolle Farbe und schmeckte leicht und frisch.

text:
We had a reservation for 15 people and were spontaneously joined by two more guests. The team reacted immediately and proactively, providing an additional table without hesitation – a perfect start to the evening.

The menu offers a diverse selection that truly caters to every taste, and the overall quality of the dishes was very high thanks to the well-designed and clearly laid-out menu. There were a few minor issues – likely due to the size of our order and the fully occupied terrace. For example, the asparagus could perhaps have cooked for one or two minutes longer, although this is, of course, subjective. Even a small hair in the food was forgivable, as the compensation was exemplary and exceeded our expectations.

The professional, attentive, and exceptionally friendly service deserves special mention. Despite the terrace being full, the entire service team maintained a clear overview at all times, fulfilled every request, and even took the time for friendly small talk. The restaurant manager was also present, open to questions, and actively sought conversation – a sign of true hospitality.

Our heartfelt thanks go to the amazing kitchen crew for the wonderful food, and especially to our server Claire and the entire service team, who provided helpful and collegial support in every way.

Please keep up the great work! Trust in your charming hospitality – we'll definitely be back.

Fischer & Lustig is absolutely worth a visit.

Thank you so much!
originalText:
Wir waren als Gruppe von 15 Personen reserviert und wurden spontan noch um 2 weitere Gäste ergänzt. Das Team reagierte sofort lösungsorientiert und stellte ohne Zögern einen zusätzlichen Tisch bereit – ein gelungener Start in den Abend.

Die Speisekarte bietet eine vielseitige Auswahl, die wirklich jeden Geschmack trifft und die Qualität der Gerichte war insgesamt sehr hoch dank der ausgeklügelten und übersichtlichen Speisekarte. Ein paar kleine Mängel gab es – vermutlich bedingt durch die Größe unserer Bestellung und die vollständig belegte Terrasse. So hätte der Spargel für unseren Geschmack vielleicht 1–2 Minuten länger garen können, wobei das natürlich subjektiv ist. Selbst ein kleines Haar im Essen war verzeihlich, da die Wiedergutmachung absolut vorbildlich und über unseren Erwartungen lag.

Besonders hervorzuheben ist der professionelle, aufmerksame und ausgesprochen freundliche Service. Trotz voll belegter Terrasse behielt das gesamte Serviceteam jederzeit den Überblick, erfüllte jeden Wunsch und nahm sich sogar Zeit für herzlichen Smalltalk. Auch der Restaurantmanager war präsent, offen für Rückfragen und suchte aktiv das Gespräch – ein Zeichen echter Gastgeberkultur.

Unser Dank gilt von Herzen der leistungsstarken Küchencrew für das zauberhafte Essen sowie ganz besonders unserer Servicekraft Claire und dem gesamten Serviceteam, die sie hilfsbereit und kollegial in allen Belangen unterstützte.

Macht unbedingt weiter so! Vertraut auf eure charmante Gastgebermentalität – wir kommen sehr gern wieder.

Fischer & Lustig ist definitiv eine Empfehlung wert.
Vielen lieben Dank!

I asked him why I had to wait 20 minutes, to which he replied that he had simply forgotten—without even an apology. He explained that he had forgotten because of the large number of customers. text:
I honestly only recommend Saravanaa Bhavan for South Indian dishes. Everything else feels like it’s just on the menu to make it look bigger. If you’re craving North Indian food like aloo puri or a good cup of chai, you’re much better off going to a proper North Indian restaurant.

Even the South Indian food has become inconsistent. The sambar is almost always served lukewarm instead of hot, and the medu vada taste like they’ve been made well in advance and are served cold rather than fresh.

Overall, it’s okay if you’re sticking to a few South Indian staples, but don’t expect much from the rest of the menu. There’s definitely room for improvement in both food quality and serving temperature.

placeAddress: Saravanaa Bhavan, Potsdamer Platz 5, 10785 Berlin, Germany
placeDescription: Long-running international chain serving up South Indian vegetarian dishes, including dosas.
text:
Saravanaa Bhavan in Berlin is one of my go-to places when I’m craving South Indian food. It’s rare to find a spot that really gets those familiar flavours right, but this place comes close in a comforting way.

The dosas are what I keep going back for, and the thalis always feel satisfying and well-balanced. The idlis in sambar are another favourite, simple but really good when you want something warm and familiar.

It’s one of those places that makes you happy just by being consistent and dependable whenever the craving hits. Sometimes it can get quite busy, so ordering and food service may take a little longer. Seating can also feel a bit tight when the place is full, but they’re usually helpful if you ask to move to a more comfortable spot.

text:
Positive: the location is convenient and in a heavy foot traffic area.

Negatives: Upon entering and being assigned an unpleasant seat I tried to move tables. The restaurant was virtually empty but the waitress got mad at me and made me return to my seat.

The food was reheated, low quality, and made me sick afterwards. The rice paneer pulao was drowning in reheated oil and had a funky smell to it. The yoghurt sauce or curd tasted as it had been left out of the refrigerator for some time and not handled properly.

Meanwhile the dosa masala was an enormous dry, overcooked and brittle dosa with a tiny amount of potatoes which were also old, slimy and stale. The energy in the restaurant is not the best coming from the managers and workers and this is reflected on the food that is being provided.

Having lived in Berlin for some years now I consider this a tourist trap. I will not be coming back to this restaurant and recommend other dosa places with high quality and fresh ingredients.

text:
How can you start your Sunday off right?

Off to HeimWerk! Around 10 a.m., it wasn't very crowded, and I was able to enjoy a wonderful, peaceful start to the day.

I immediately felt welcome thanks to the truly charming and friendly Sarah, who was always there at the right time to ask if I needed anything. Thank you, Sarah, for the lovely, warm, and atmospheric start to the day!

A nice, varied playlist further contributed to the cozy atmosphere.

And of course, I mustn't forget the food: The breakfast burger and the yogurt were a fantastic combination.

Considering that Hackescher Markt is quite a touristy area and therefore a bit pricey, the value for money here was absolutely fine and justified.

Thank you for the wonderful visit and the great start to the day! ❤️

P.S. For solo diners, smaller tables with fewer seats might be even cozier... but that's just nitpicking! 😜
originalText:

Das Essen will ich natürlich nicht vergessen: Der Frühstücksburger und der Joghurt waren wirklich eine super Kombi.
Und dafür, dass der Hackesche Markt ein schon Recht touristischer Ort und dementsprechend etwas höherpreisig unterwegs ist, so war das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis hier absolut OK und gerechtfertigt.
Danke für den wunderbaren Besuch und den tollen Start in den Tag!❤️

We're also sorry to hear that you found the food too bland for your taste and that the service did not leave a more positive impression. We will share your feedback with our team, as providing a welcoming and attentive experience is very important to us.

Thank you again for your honest review. We appreciate your feedback and will use it to continue improving.

Your Team at HeimWerk

text: Our cruise boat docked at the closest port to Berlin, about a 2-hour drive, but we were not going to be in that part of Germany and not make it to Berlin. So, our group of 10 booked a private guide and drivers and set out. After the initial drive and some touring, we needed lunch and our guide took us to Gendarmerie. First off, it is one of the coolest restaurants inside that I have ever seen. The large piece of art that stretches the width of the restaurant is outstanding and eye catching. There are also replica pieces of the Berlin wall used as art and a series of giant portraits of famous German actors and actresses along with John F. Kennedy. Strange combination. We were seated at a long table. Our server was excellent and very entertaining for this table full of Americans. I can only speak of the two dishes that my wife and I ordered. I had the fried pike-perch fillet, but it was served on fresh local white asparagus which was in season and highly recommended. I can say without question that it was the largest asparagus I have ever seen in my life. Full of flavor with a sauce on the side. Trouble with it was that there was too much and much of it was quite tough. I prefer my asparagus thin not tree trunks. The fish was good but a bit dry so the sauce was welcome. My wife had Konigsberger meatballs with red beetroot and mashed potatoes all in a cream sauce. They are not shy about their sauces here as the photos indicate. But, the meal was very good. At the end, knowing we wanted to divide the check, the server merely had us come to the counter a couple at a time and simply tell him what we had to eat. It all added up so we were good. End review is that it was a great location, but the food was not outstanding at all. If given a greater scale, the review would be a solid 3.5.

text:
We dined at the Gendarmerie restaurant in the capital and ordered Wiener Schnitzel and asparagus salad.

The schnitzel was truly delicious, and we were especially surprised by the portion size – quite large and definitely more than enough. The breading was beautifully crispy, and the meat was juicy. The asparagus salad was also very fresh and flavorful, a lovely light complement to the schnitzel.

Of course, the prices here are on the higher end. We paid around €100 for two people, including drinks. However, considering the location, the lovely ambiance, the quality of the food, and the generous portions, we found the price absolutely fair.

The service was friendly, quick, and attentive without being intrusive. The restaurant is very clean, quiet, and comfortably furnished, making it easy to sit and have a conversation. The restrooms were also clean, and the wait for the food was perfectly acceptable.

Overall, a really good experience. If you're willing to spend a little more, you'll find good food, a pleasant atmosphere, and attentive service here. I would definitely come back.
